title.zh: 卷七十二 列傳第二十二: 虞世南 李百藥 褚亮
title.en: Volume 72 Biographies 22: Yu Shinian, Li Baiyao, Chuliang
title.raw: 卷七十二 列傳第二十二: 虞世南 李百藥 褚亮 Volume 72 Biographies 22: Yu Shinian, Li Baiyao, Chuliang

sentences.zh: 虞世南 李百藥 子安期

translations.literal: Yu Shinan, Li Baiyao, and His Son Anqi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shinan; Li Baiyao; and His Son Anqi

sentences.zh: 褚亮 劉孝孫 李玄道 李守素附

translations.literal: Chuliang, Liu Xiaosun, Li Xuandao, with Li Shousu appended
translations.idiomatic: Chuliang; Liu Xiaosun; Li Xuandao; with Li Shousu appended

sentences.zh: 虞世南，字伯施，越州餘姚人，隋內史侍郎世基弟也。

translations.literal: Yu Shinan, styled Boshi, was a native of Yuyao in Yuezhou, and was the younger brother of Yu Shiji, Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shinan, whose style was Boshi, came from Yuyao in Yuezhou. He was the younger brother of Yu Shiji, Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 祖檢，梁始興王諮議；

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian was adviser to the Prince of Shixing of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jian had served as adviser to the Prince of Shixing under the Liang;

sentences.zh: 父荔，陳太子中庶子，俱有重名。

translations.literal: his father Li was Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince of Chen; both enjoyed great renown.
translations.idiomatic: his father Li had been Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince of Chen. Both men enjoyed great renown.

sentences.zh: 叔父寄，陳中書侍郎，無子，以世南繼後，故字曰伯施。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother Ji was Vice Director of the Secretariat of Chen; having no son, he adopted Shinian as heir, hence his style Boshi.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Ji had been Vice Director of the Secretariat under Chen. Having no son of his own, he adopted Shinian as his heir, which is why his style was Boshi, "Heir."

sentences.zh: 世南性沈靜寡慾，篤志勤學，少與兄世基受學於吳郡顧野王，經十餘年，精思不倦，或累旬不盥櫛。

translations.literal: Shinian was by nature calm and quiet with few desires, devoted in spirit and diligent in study. In youth he and his elder brother Shiji studied under Gu Yewang of Wu Commandery for more than ten years, applying themselves without weariness; at times he went many days without washing or combing his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Shinian was calm and reserved by nature, with few worldly desires, and he pursued learning with single-minded devotion. As a youth he and his elder brother Shiji studied under Gu Yewang of Wu Commandery for more than ten years, thinking deeply without flagging; at times he would go many days without washing or combing his hair.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，常祖述徐陵，陵亦言世南得己之意。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composition and often followed the style of Xu Ling; Xu Ling also said that Shinian had grasped his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at literary composition and often took Xu Ling as his model; Xu Ling himself said that Shinian had caught his meaning.

sentences.zh: 又同郡沙門智永，善王羲之書，世南師焉，妙得其體，由是聲名籍甚。

translations.literal: A monk of his native commandery named Zhiyong excelled in the calligraphy of Wang Xizhi; Shinian studied with him and mastered the essentials of that style, whence his reputation became very great.
translations.idiomatic: A monk of the same commandery, Zhiyong, was skilled in the calligraphy of Wang Xizhi. Shinian studied under him and mastered its essential forms, and from that time his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，荔卒，世南尚幼，哀毀殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: During the Tianchen era his father Li died; Shinian was still young and in mourning was so stricken with grief he nearly could not bear the rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianchen reign his father Li died. Shinian was still young, and his grief in mourning was so overwhelming that he nearly could not endure the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝知其二子博學，每遣中使至其家將護之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen knew the two brothers were learned and repeatedly sent palace emissaries to their home to tend and protect them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Chen knew that the two brothers were deeply learned and repeatedly sent palace envoys to their home to look after them.

sentences.zh: 及服闋，召為建安王法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was summoned and appointed Army Assistant under the Director of Justice for the Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete, he was summoned and appointed Army Assistant in the Office of Justice for the Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 寄陷於陳寶應，在閩、越中，世南雖除喪，猶布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: Ji had been trapped by Chen Baoying in Min and Yue; though Shinian's mourning period had ended, he still wore plain cloth and ate simple food.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Ji had been trapped by Chen Baoying in Min and Yue. Although Shinian's mourning period had ended, he still wore plain cloth and ate simple fare.

sentences.zh: 至太建末，寶應破，寄還，方令世南釋布食肉。

translations.literal: Not until late in the Taijian reign, when Baoying was destroyed and Ji returned, did he allow Shinian to set aside plain cloth and eat meat again.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the end of the Taijian reign, when Baoying was defeated and Ji returned, did he permit Shinian to put off plain dress and eat meat again.

sentences.zh: 至德初，除西陽王友。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide reign he was appointed Friend of the Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhide reign he was appointed Friend of the Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 陳滅，與世基同入長安，俱有重名，時人方之二陸。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he and Shiji entered Chang'an together; both had great fame, and people at the time compared them to the two Lu brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he and Shiji entered Chang'an together. Both enjoyed great renown, and people of the time compared them to the two Lu brothers.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝在籓，聞其名，與秦王俊辟書交至，以母老固辭，晉王令使者追之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was still Prince of Jin, he heard of Shinian's name and exchanged letters of appointment with Prince Qin Jun; Shinian firmly declined on account of his aged mother, so the Prince of Jin ordered an envoy to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Yang was still Prince of Jin, he heard of Shinian's reputation, and letters of appointment from him and from Prince Qin Jun arrived one after another. Shinian firmly declined on account of his aged mother, so the Prince of Jin ordered an envoy to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 大業初，累授秘書郎，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye reign he was repeatedly appointed Secretary of the Palace Library and then promoted to Attendant for Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye reign he was repeatedly appointed Secretary of the Palace Library and was later promoted to Attendant for Drafting.

sentences.zh: 時世基當朝貴盛，妻子被服擬於王者。

translations.literal: At that time Shiji held high office at court and was flourishing; his wife and children dressed in a style rivaling that of kings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shiji held power at court and was at the height of his glory; his wife and children dressed in a style rivaling that of royalty.

sentences.zh: 世南雖同居，而躬履勤儉，不失素業。

translations.literal: Although Shinian lived under the same roof, he himself practiced diligence and frugality and did not abandon his former modest station.
translations.idiomatic: Although Shinian lived under the same roof, he himself practiced diligence and frugality and did not abandon his former modest way of life.

sentences.zh: 及至隋滅，宇文化及弒逆之際，世基為內史侍郎，將被誅，世南抱持號泣，請以身代，化及不納，因哀毀骨立，時人稱焉。

translations.literal: When the Sui fell, at the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Shiji was Vice Director of the Secretariat and was to be executed; Shinian embraced him weeping and begged to die in his brother's place. Huaji did not accept, and Shinian grieved until he was wasted to the bone—people at the time praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui fell, at the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Shiji was Vice Director of the Secretariat and was about to be executed. Shinian embraced him, weeping, and begged to die in his brother's place. Huaji would not accept, and Shinian grieved until he was wasted to the bone. People of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 從化及至聊城，又陷於竇建德，偽授黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Following Huaji to Liaocheng, he fell into the hands of Dou Jiande, who falsely appointed him Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Huaji to Liaocheng and then fell into the hands of Dou Jiande, who falsely appointed him Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 八年，隴右山崩，大蛇屢見，山東及江淮多大水。

translations.literal: In the eighth year mountains collapsed in Longyou, great serpents were repeatedly seen, and Shandong and the Huai and Yangzi regions suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year mountains collapsed in Longyou, great serpents were seen again and again, and Shandong and the Huai and Yangzi regions suffered severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 太宗以問世南，對曰：「春秋時山崩，晉侯召伯宗而問焉，對曰：『國主山川，故山川崩竭，君為之不舉，降服、乘縵、徹樂、出次、祝幣以禮焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong questioned Shinian about it. He replied: "In the time of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a mountain collapsed, the Marquis of Jin summoned Bozong and questioned him. He answered: 'The state holds the mountains and rivers in trust, so when mountains and rivers collapse and are exhausted, the ruler for this reason does not hold feasts, wears humble dress, rides in an unadorned carriage, reduces music, leaves the palace temporarily, and offers ritual oblation with silken gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong asked Shinian about these signs. He replied: "In the age of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a mountain collapsed, the Marquis of Jin summoned Bozong and questioned him. Bozong answered: 'The state holds the mountains and rivers in trust. When mountains and rivers collapse and fail, the ruler for this reason suspends feasts, wears humble dress, rides in an unadorned carriage, reduces music, leaves the palace temporarily, and offers ritual gifts according to propriety.

sentences.zh: 』梁山，晉所主也，晉侯從之，故得無害。

translations.literal: 'Yanzi Mountain was the domain held by Jin; the Marquis of Jin followed this counsel, and therefore escaped harm.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Yanzi Mountain was the domain held by Jin. The Marquis of Jin followed this counsel, and therefore escaped harm.'

sentences.zh: 漢文帝元年，齊、楚地二十九山同日崩，水大出，令郡國無來貢獻，施惠於天下，遠近歡洽，亦不為災。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, twenty-nine mountains in Qi and Chu lands collapsed on the same day and great floods issued forth. He ordered the commanderies and principalities to send no tribute and showed kindness throughout the realm; far and near rejoiced together, and it did not become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, twenty-nine mountains in the lands of Qi and Chu collapsed on the same day and great floods broke out. He ordered the commanderies and principalities to send no tribute and showed kindness throughout the realm. Far and near rejoiced together, and no calamity resulted.

sentences.zh: 後漢靈帝時，青蛇見御座。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ling of Later Han a green serpent appeared on the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling of Later Han a green serpent appeared on the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝時，大蛇長三百步，見齊地，經市入朝。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui of Jin a great serpent three hundred paces long appeared in Qi territory, passing through markets and entering the court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui of Jin a great serpent three hundred paces long appeared in the land of Qi, passing through markets and entering the court.

sentences.zh: 案蛇宜在草野，而入市朝，所以可為怪耳。

translations.literal: Considering the matter, serpents belong in wilderness and grassland; that they entered markets and court is what made them strange.
translations.idiomatic: Serpents belong in wilderness and grassland; that they entered markets and court is what made them strange.

sentences.zh: 今蛇見山澤，蓋深山大澤必有龍蛇，亦不足怪也。

translations.literal: Now that serpents are seen in mountains and marshes, surely in great mountains and great marshes there are always dragons and serpents—this too is not enough to be considered strange.
translations.idiomatic: Now that serpents are seen in mountains and marshes, it is only natural, for great mountains and great marshes always harbor dragons and serpents. This is hardly worth calling strange.

sentences.zh: 又山東足雨，雖則其常，然陰淫過久，恐有冤獄，宜省繫囚，庶幾或當天意。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shandong has ample rain; though this is normal, if yin dampness lasts too long there may be unjust imprisonments. It would be fitting to review those held in bonds; perhaps this may accord with Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Shandong has had ample rain. Though that is normal, if excessive dampness persists too long, there may be unjust imprisonments. It would be fitting to review those held in prison; perhaps this may accord with Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 且妖不勝德，唯修德可以銷變。

translations.literal: Moreover, omens cannot overcome virtue; only by cultivating virtue can these signs be transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, portents cannot overcome virtue; only by cultivating virtue can these signs be dispelled.

sentences.zh: 」太宗以為然，因遣使者賑恤飢餒，申理獄訟，多所原宥。

translations.literal: " The Emperor considered this correct and therefore sent envoys to relieve famine and hunger, examine lawsuits, and grant much forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed and therefore sent envoys to relieve famine and hunger, examine lawsuits, and grant much forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 後有星孛於虛、危，歷於氐，百餘日乃滅。

translations.literal: Later a broom star blazed in Xu and Wei, passed through Di, and only after more than a hundred days vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Later a broom star appeared in Xu and Wei, passed through Di, and only after more than a hundred days did it vanish.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂群臣曰：「天見彗星，是何妖也？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to his ministers: "Heaven has shown a comet—what omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to his ministers: "Heaven has shown a comet. What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 」世南曰：「昔齊景公時有彗星見，公問晏嬰，對曰：『穿池沼畏不深，起台榭畏不高，行刑罰畏不重，是以天見彗為公誡耳。

translations.literal: " Shinian said: "In former times, under Duke Jing of Qi, a comet appeared. The duke asked Yan Ying, who answered: 'You fear your pools and marshes are not deep enough, your terraces and pavilions not high enough, your punishments not severe enough—therefore Heaven shows the comet to warn you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: " Shinian said: "In former times, under Duke Jing of Qi, a comet appeared. The duke asked Yan Ying, who answered: 'You fear your pools and marshes are not deep enough, your terraces and pavilions not high enough, your punishments not severe enough. That is why Heaven shows the comet to warn you, my lord.

sentences.zh: 』景公懼而修德，後十六日而星沒。

translations.literal: ' The duke took fright and cultivated virtue; sixteen days later the star vanished.
translations.idiomatic: ' The duke took fright and cultivated virtue, and sixteen days later the star vanished.

sentences.zh: 臣聞『天時不如地利，地利不如人和』，若德義不修，雖獲麟鳳，終是無補；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that 'favorable season is less than terrain, and terrain is less than human accord.' If virtue and righteousness are not cultivated, even though one obtain qilin and phoenixes, in the end it is of no avail;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that 'favorable season is less than terrain, and terrain is less than human accord.' If virtue and righteousness are not cultivated, even if one obtains qilin and phoenixes, in the end it will be of no avail;

sentences.zh: 但政事無闕，雖有災星，何損於時？

translations.literal: but if governance is without fault, what harm can disaster stars do the age?
translations.idiomatic: but if governance is without fault, what harm can disaster stars do the age?

sentences.zh: 然願陛下勿以功高古人而自矜伐，勿以太平漸久而自驕怠，慎終如始，彗星雖見，未足為憂。

translations.literal: Yet your servant wishes that Your Majesty not pride yourself on achievements surpassing the ancients, not grow arrogant and negligent as peace lengthens, and be as careful at the end as at the beginning—then though the comet is seen, it is not enough to be a cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I urge Your Majesty not to pride yourself on achievements surpassing the ancients, not to grow arrogant and negligent as peace lengthens, and to be as careful at the end as at the beginning. Then though the comet is seen, it need not be a cause for worry.

sentences.zh: 」太宗斂容謂曰：「吾之撫國，良無景公之過。

translations.literal: " The Emperor composed his countenance and said: "In governing the realm I truly have no fault like Duke Jing's.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor composed himself and said: "In governing the realm I truly have no fault like Duke Jing's.

sentences.zh: 但吾才弱冠舉義兵，年二十四平天下，未三十而居大位，自謂三代以降，撥亂之主，莫臻於此。

translations.literal: But from a tender age I raised the banner of righteous warfare; at twenty-four I pacified the realm, and before thirty I held the supreme position. I consider that among lords who quelled disorder since the Three Dynasties, none has reached this.
translations.idiomatic: But from a tender age I raised the banner of righteous warfare. At twenty-four I pacified the realm, and before thirty I held the supreme position. I consider that among lords who quelled disorder since the Three Dynasties, none has reached this.

sentences.zh: 重以薛舉之驍雄，宋金剛之鷙猛，竇建德跨河北，王世充據洛陽，當此之時，足為勍敵，皆為我所擒。

translations.literal: Add to this the fierce valor of Xue Ju, the fierce ferocity of Song Jingang, Dou Jiande spanning Hebei, and Wang Shichong holding Luoyang—at that time they were fully formidable foes, yet all were captured by me.
translations.idiomatic: Add to this the fierce valor of Xue Ju, the savage might of Song Jingang, Dou Jiande spanning Hebei, and Wang Shichong holding Luoyang. At that time they were truly formidable foes, yet all were captured by me.

sentences.zh: 及逢家難，復決意安社稷，遂登九五，降服北夷，吾頗有自矜之意，以輕天下之士，此吾之罪也。

translations.literal: When I encountered family strife I again resolved to secure the altars of soil and grain, ascended the throne, and subjugated the northern barbarians. I have had some pride in myself and have slighted the worthies under heaven—this is my fault.
translations.idiomatic: When I encountered family strife I again resolved to secure the altars of state, ascended the throne, and subjugated the northern barbarians. I have taken some pride in myself and have slighted the worthies under heaven. This is my fault.

sentences.zh: 上天見變，良為是乎？

translations.literal: Has Heaven shown these signs truly for this reason?
translations.idiomatic: Has Heaven shown these signs truly for this reason?

sentences.zh: 秦始皇平六國，隋煬帝富四海，既驕且逸，一朝而敗，吾亦何得自驕也。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang unified the six states and Emperor Yang of Sui enriched the four seas; each through pride and indulgence fell in a single morning—how can I myself grow arrogant?
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang unified the six states and Emperor Yang of Sui enriched the four seas, yet each through pride and indulgence fell in a single morning. How can I myself grow arrogant?

sentences.zh: 言念於此，不覺惕焉震懼。

translations.literal: When I reflect on this, I cannot but feel apprehension and awe.
translations.idiomatic: When I reflect on this, I cannot but feel apprehension and awe.

sentences.zh: 」四月，康國獻獅子，詔世南為之賦，命編之東觀，辭多不載。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month Kang kingdom presented a lion; he ordered Shinian to compose a fu for it and had it compiled in the Eastern Archive—most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month the state of Kang presented a lion. He ordered Shinian to compose a fu for it and had it compiled in the Eastern Archive, but most of the text is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 後高祖崩，有詔山陵制度，准漢長陵故事，務從隆厚。

translations.literal: Later, when Gaozu died, an edict on tomb regulations followed the precedent of Emperor Wu's Changling, aiming at lavish scale.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gaozu died, an edict on tomb regulations followed the precedent of Emperor Wu's Changling, aiming at lavish scale.

sentences.zh: 程限既促，功役勞弊。

translations.literal: The deadline was short and the labor burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: The deadline was short and the labor burdensome.

sentences.zh: 世南上封事諫曰：

translations.literal: Shinian submitted a sealed memorial remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: Shinian submitted a sealed memorial remonstrating:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之聖帝明王所以薄葬者，非不欲崇高光顯，珍寶具物，以厚其親。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the reason ancient sage emperors and enlightened kings practiced modest burial was not that they did not wish splendor and brilliance, treasures and full accoutrements, to enrich their kin.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the reason ancient sage emperors and enlightened kings practiced modest burial was not that they did not wish splendor, brilliance, treasures, and full accoutrements to enrich their kin.

sentences.zh: 然審而言之，高墳厚壟，珍物畢備，此適所以為親之累，非曰孝也。

translations.literal: Yet when examined closely, high mounds and thick earthworks with treasures fully prepared are precisely what burden one's kin; this is not called filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when examined closely, high mounds and thick earthworks with treasures fully prepared are precisely what burden one's kin. This is not called filial piety.

sentences.zh: 是以深思遠慮，安於菲薄，以為長久萬代之計，割其常情以定耳。

translations.literal: Therefore with deep thought and far-reaching consideration they settled on modesty, taking it as a plan for lasting benefit through ten thousand generations, restraining ordinary feeling to fix policy.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with deep thought and far-reaching consideration they settled on modesty, taking it as a plan for lasting benefit through ten thousand generations, restraining ordinary feeling to fix policy.

sentences.zh: 昔漢成帝造延、昌二陵，制度甚厚，功費甚多。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Cheng of Han built the Yan and Chang tombs; the regulations were very lavish and the labor and expense very great.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Cheng of Han built the Yan and Chang tombs. The regulations were very lavish and the labor and expense very great.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫劉向上書，其言深切，皆合事理。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Opinion Official Liu Xiang submitted a memorial; his words were profound and all accorded with reason and affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Opinion Official Liu Xiang submitted a memorial whose words were profound and all accorded with reason and affairs.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「孝文居霸陵，淒愴悲懷，顧謂群臣曰：『嗟乎！

translations.literal: Its gist says: "When Emperor Wen dwelt at Baling he gazed mournfully and with sorrow, turned to his ministers and said: 'Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Its gist says: "When Emperor Wen dwelt at Baling he gazed mournfully and with sorrow, turned to his ministers and said: 'Alas!

sentences.zh: 以北山石為槨，用纻絮斮陳漆其間，豈可動哉？

translations.literal: Let the coffin be of northern mountain stone, with ramie stuffing chopped fine and lacquered within—surely it could not be moved?'
translations.idiomatic: Let the coffin be of northern mountain stone, with ramie stuffing chopped fine and lacquered within. Surely it could not be moved?'

sentences.zh: 』張釋之進曰：『使其中有可欲，雖錮南山猶有隙；

translations.literal: ' Zhang Shizhi advanced and said: 'If within there is something desirable, though the southern mountains were bound with bronze there would still be gaps;
translations.idiomatic: ' Zhang Shizhi advanced and said: 'If within there is something desirable, though the southern mountains were bound with bronze there would still be gaps;

sentences.zh: 使其中無可欲，雖無石槨，又何戚焉！

translations.literal: if within there is nothing desirable, though there were no stone coffin, what sorrow could there be!'
translations.idiomatic: if within there is nothing desirable, though there were no stone coffin, what sorrow could there be!'

sentences.zh: 』夫死者無終極，而國家有廢興，釋之所言，為無窮計也。

translations.literal: ' The dead have no end, while states rise and fall; what Zhang said planned for eternity.
translations.idiomatic: ' The dead have no end, while states rise and fall. What Zhang said planned for eternity.

sentences.zh: 孝文寤焉，遂以薄葬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen took counsel and therefore adopted modest burial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen took counsel and therefore adopted modest burial.

sentences.zh: 」又漢氏之法，人君在位，三分天下貢賦，以一分入山陵。

translations.literal: " Moreover, by Han law, while a ruler held the throne one third of the tribute of the realm was allotted, and one part of that went to the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, by Han law, while a ruler held the throne one third of the tribute of the realm was allotted, and one part of that went to the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 武帝歷年長久，比葬，陵中不復容物，霍光暗於大體，奢侈過度。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu reigned for many years; when he was buried the tomb could hold no more goods. Huo Guang, dull to the larger principle, exceeded in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu reigned for many years. When he was buried the tomb could hold no more goods. Huo Guang, dull to the larger principle, exceeded in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 其後至更始之敗，赤眉賊入長安，破茂陵取物，猶不能盡。

translations.literal: Later, at the defeat of Emperor Gengshi, the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an, broke Maoling, and took its goods yet could not exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the defeat of Emperor Gengshi, the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an, broke Maoling, and took its goods yet could not exhaust them.

sentences.zh: 無故聚斂百姓，為盜之用，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: Uselessly taxing the people to serve robbers—this was utterly pointless.
translations.idiomatic: Uselessly taxing the people to serve robbers—this was utterly pointless.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝於首陽東為壽陵，作終制，其略曰：「昔堯葬壽陵，因山為體，無封樹，無立寢殿園邑，為棺槨足以藏骨，為衣衾足以朽肉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei east of Shouyang made his longevity tomb and composed final instructions. Their gist says: "In former times Yao was buried at Shouyang, using the mountain as the body; no mound was planted, no resting hall or park enclosure established. The coffin was enough to hold the bones, the clothing enough to rot the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei east of Shouyang made his longevity tomb and composed final instructions. Their gist says: "In former times Yao was buried at Shouyang, using the mountain as the body. No mound was planted, no resting hall or park enclosure established. The coffin was enough to hold the bones, the clothing enough to rot the flesh.

sentences.zh: 吾營此不食之地，欲使易代之後，不知其處，無藏金銀銅鐵，一以瓦器。

translations.literal: I have sought this land that will not be cultivated, wishing that after dynasties change none will know the site, storing no gold, silver, copper, or iron—only earthenware throughout.
translations.idiomatic: I have sought this land that will not be cultivated, wishing that after dynasties change none will know the site, storing no gold, silver, copper, or iron—only earthenware throughout.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有不亡之國，無有不發之墓，至乃燒取玉匣金縷，骸骨並盡，乃不重痛哉！

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present there has been no state that did not perish, no tomb that was not opened; even to the point of burning jade cases with gold thread until bones were destroyed together—is this not a double pain!
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present there has been no state that did not perish, no tomb that was not opened. Even to the point of burning jade cases with gold thread until bones were destroyed together—is this not a double pain!

sentences.zh: 若違詔妄有變改，吾為戮屍於地下，死而重死，不忠不孝，使魂而有知，將不福汝。

translations.literal: Whoever against the edict recklessly alters matters, I would be dismembered corpses underground, dying again after death, disloyal and unfilial—if the soul has knowledge, it will not bless you.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever against the edict recklessly alters matters, I would be dismembered corpses underground, dying again after death, disloyal and unfilial. If the soul has knowledge, it will not bless you.

sentences.zh: 以為永制，藏之宗廟。

translations.literal: Let this be taken as perpetual law and deposited in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be taken as perpetual law and deposited in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 」魏文帝此制，可謂達於事矣。

translations.literal: " This regulation of Emperor Wen of Wei may be called penetrating in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " This regulation of Emperor Wen of Wei may be called penetrating in affairs.

sentences.zh: 向使陛下德止如秦、漢之君，臣則緘口而已，不敢有言。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty's virtue reached only the rulers of Qin and Han, your servant would keep silent and dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's virtue reached only the rulers of Qin and Han, your servant would keep silent and dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 伏見聖德高遠，堯、舜猶所不逮，而俯與秦、漢之君同為奢泰，舍堯、舜、殷、周之節儉，此臣所以尤戚也。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that sacred virtue is lofty and far-reaching, beyond even Yao and Shun, yet you stoop to share extravagance with the rulers of Qin and Han, abandoning the frugality of Yao, Shun, Yin, and Zhou—this is why your servant is especially grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed that sacred virtue is lofty and far-reaching, beyond even Yao and Shun, yet you stoop to share extravagance with the rulers of Qin and Han, abandoning the frugality of Yao, Shun, Yin, and Zhou. This is why your servant is especially grieved.

sentences.zh: 今為丘壟如此，其內雖不藏珍寶，亦無益也。

translations.literal: Now to make a tomb mound like this—even though no treasures are stored within, it is still of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Now to make a tomb mound like this—even though no treasures are stored within, it is still of no benefit.

sentences.zh: 萬代之後，但見高墳大墓，豈謂無金玉耶？

translations.literal: Ten thousand generations hence, when people see only a high mound and great tomb, will they not suppose there is gold and jade within?
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand generations hence, when people see only a high mound and great tomb, will they not suppose there is gold and jade within?

sentences.zh: 臣之愚計，以為漢文霸陵，既因山勢，雖不起墳，自然高顯。

translations.literal: Your servant's humble plan is that the Baling of Han Wen, following the mountain's shape, though no mound is raised, is naturally high and prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's humble plan is that the Baling of Han Wen, following the mountain's shape, though no mound is raised, is naturally high and prominent.

sentences.zh: 今之所卜，地勢即平，不可不起，宜依《白虎通》所陳周制，為三仞之墳，其方中制度，事事減少。

translations.literal: The ground now divined is level and a mound cannot but be raised. It would be fitting to follow the Zhou system set forth in the Baihu tong, making a mound of three ren; in the central square and in every regulation, reduce each measure.
translations.idiomatic: The ground now divined is level and a mound cannot but be raised. It would be fitting to follow the Zhou system set forth in the Baihu tong, making a mound of three ren, and in the central square and in every regulation to reduce each measure.

sentences.zh: 事竟之日，刻石於陵側，明丘封大小高下之式。

translations.literal: When the work is completed, inscribe stone beside the tomb showing the form of the mound's size and height.
translations.idiomatic: When the work is completed, inscribe stone beside the tomb showing the form of the mound's size and height.

sentences.zh: 明器所須，皆以瓦木，合於禮文，一不得用金銀銅鐵。

translations.literal: Goods for the dead should all be of tile and wood, in accord with ritual texts; none may use gold, silver, copper, or iron.
translations.idiomatic: Goods for the dead should all be of tile and wood, in accord with ritual texts. None may use gold, silver, copper, or iron.

sentences.zh: 使萬代子孫，並皆遵奉，一通藏之宗廟，豈不美乎！

translations.literal: Let descendants through ten thousand generations all observe and follow this; deposit one copy in the ancestral temple—how fine that would be!
translations.idiomatic: Let descendants through ten thousand generations all observe and follow this. Deposit one copy in the ancestral temple—how fine that would be!

sentences.zh: 且臣下除服用三十六日，已依霸陵，今為墳壟，又以長陵為法，恐非所宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, ministers' mourning garments are for thirty-six days, already following the Baling precedent; now for the tomb mound to take Changling as the model is perhaps inapt.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ministers' mourning garments are for thirty-six days, already following the Baling precedent. Now for the tomb mound to take Changling as the model is perhaps inapt.

sentences.zh: 伏願深覽古今，為長久之慮，臣之赤心，唯願萬歲之後，神道常安，陛下孝名，揚於無窮耳。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that you deeply view past and present for long-term planning. Your servant's loyal heart wishes only that after ten thousand years the spirit way be always secure and Your Majesty's name for filial piety shine without end.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes that you deeply view past and present for long-term planning. Your servant's loyal heart wishes only that after ten thousand years the spirit way be always secure and Your Majesty's name for filial piety shine without end.

sentences.zh: 書奏不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 世南又上疏曰：「漢家即位之初，便營陵墓，近者十餘歲，遠者五十年方始成就。

translations.literal: Shinian again submitted a memorial saying: "The Han at the beginning of enthronement began tomb works; the near took more than ten years, the far fifty years before completion.
translations.idiomatic: Shinian again submitted a memorial saying: "The Han at the beginning of enthronement began tomb works. The near took more than ten years, the far fifty years before completion.

sentences.zh: 今以數月之間而造數十年之事，其於人力，亦已勞矣。

translations.literal: Now to do in a few months what took decades—the burden on human labor is already severe.
translations.idiomatic: Now to do in a few months what took decades—the burden on human labor is already severe.

sentences.zh: 又漢家大郡五十萬戶，即目人眾未及往時，而功役與之一等，此臣所以致疑也。

translations.literal: Moreover, a great commandery of Han had five hundred thousand households; at present the population has not reached former times, yet the labor equals that era—this is why your servant raises doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a great commandery of Han had five hundred thousand households. At present the population has not reached former times, yet the labor equals that era. This is why your servant raises doubt.

sentences.zh: 」時公卿又上奏請遵遺詔，務從節儉，因下其事付所司詳議，於是制度頗有減省焉。

translations.literal: " At that time high officials again memorialized asking to follow the late emperor's will and practice thrift; the matter was therefore sent down to the relevant offices for detailed deliberation, and the regulations were much reduced.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time high officials again memorialized asking to follow the late emperor's will and practice thrift. The matter was therefore sent down to the relevant offices for detailed deliberation, and the regulations were much reduced.

sentences.zh: 太宗後頗好獵，世南上疏諫曰：「臣聞秋獮冬狩，蓋惟恆典；

translations.literal: Later the Emperor came to favor hunting. Shinian submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that the autumn battue and winter hunt are constant precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor came to favor hunting. Shinian submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that the autumn battue and winter hunt are constant precedent;

sentences.zh: 射隼從禽，備乎前誥。

translations.literal: shooting hawks and taking game are provided for in former canons.
translations.idiomatic: shooting hawks and taking game are provided for in former canons.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下因聽覽之餘辰，順天道以殺伐，將欲躬摧班掌，親御皮軒，窮猛獸之窟穴，盡逸材於林藪。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that Your Majesty, in the remaining hours of audience, following heaven's way in killing, intends personally to crush with the palm, personally mount the leather canopy, exhaust the lairs of fierce beasts, and gather all swift quarry from forest and thicket.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects that Your Majesty, in the remaining hours of audience, following heaven's way in killing, intends personally to crush with the palm, personally mount the leather canopy, exhaust the lairs of fierce beasts, and gather all swift quarry from forest and thicket.

sentences.zh: 夷凶剪暴，以衛黎元；

translations.literal: To quell the fierce and cut down the violent, thereby protecting the black-haired people;
translations.idiomatic: To quell the fierce and cut down the violent, thereby protecting the common people;

sentences.zh: 收革擢羽，用充軍器；

translations.literal: to gather hides and pluck feathers for military gear;
translations.idiomatic: to gather hides and pluck feathers for military gear;

sentences.zh: 舉旗效獲，式遵前古。

translations.literal: to raise banners and display the catch, following the manner of former antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: to raise banners and display the catch, following the manner of former antiquity.

sentences.zh: 然黃屋之尊，金輿之貴，八方之所仰德，萬國之所繫心，清道而行，猶戒銜橛，斯蓋重慎防微，為社稷也。

translations.literal: Yet the majesty of the yellow canopy and the honor of the golden chariot are what the eight directions rely on for virtue and the ten thousand states bind their hearts to. Even on a cleared road one guards against the bit's danger—this is utmost caution and guarding against the slight, for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the majesty of the yellow canopy and the honor of the golden chariot are what the eight directions rely on for virtue and the ten thousand states bind their hearts to. Even on a cleared road one guards against the bit's danger. This is utmost caution and guarding against the slight, for the sake of the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 是以馬卿直諫於前，張昭變色於後，臣誠微淺，敢忘斯義？

translations.literal: Therefore Sima Xiangru remonstrated directly before, and Zhang Zhao changed countenance after; your servant is truly slight and shallow—how dare I forget this duty?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Sima Xiangru remonstrated directly before, and Zhang Zhao changed countenance after. Your servant is truly slight and shallow—how dare I forget this duty?

sentences.zh: 且天弧星畢，所殪已多，頒禽賜獲，皇恩亦薄。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Bow-star and the Net have already slain much; distributing game and bestowing the catch—imperial grace is also ample.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Bow-star and the Net have already slain much. In distributing game and bestowing the catch, imperial grace is also ample.

sentences.zh: 伏願時息獵車，且韜長戟，不拒芻蕘之請，降納涓澮之流，袒裼徒摶，任之群下，則貽范百王，永光萬代。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that for a time you rest the hunting chariot and sheath the long halberd, not refuse counsel from the grass cutter, accept the trickle of the rivulet, strip to wrestle and leave it to the multitude below—then you will bequeath a model to a hundred kings and eternal glory to ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes that for a time you rest the hunting chariot and sheath the long halberd, not refuse counsel from the humblest subject, accept the trickle of the rivulet, strip to wrestle and leave it to the multitude below. Then you will bequeath a model to a hundred kings and eternal glory to ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 」其有犯無隱，多此類也。

translations.literal: " His offense of speaking without concealment was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " His habit of speaking without concealment was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 太宗以是益親禮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore treated him with still greater intimacy and ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor therefore treated him with still greater intimacy and ritual respect.

sentences.zh: 嘗稱世南有五絕：一曰德行，二曰忠直，三曰博學，四曰文辭，五曰書翰。

translations.literal: He once praised that Shinian had five supreme qualities: first, virtue and conduct; second, loyalty and rectitude; third, broad learning; fourth, literary composition; fifth, calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that Shinian possessed five supreme gifts: virtue and conduct, loyalty and rectitude, broad learning, literary skill, and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又表請致仕，優制許之，仍授銀青光祿大夫、弘文館學士，祿賜防閣，並同京官職事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again memorialized requesting retirement; an excellent edict permitted it, yet he was still appointed Silver Gleam Grand Master of Glory and Scholar of the Hongwen Academy, with salary, gifts, gate guards, and duties all the same as capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again memorialized requesting retirement. An excellent edict granted his request, yet he was still appointed Silver Gleam Grand Master of Glory and Scholar of the Hongwen Academy, with salary, gifts, gate guards, and duties all matching those of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: Soon he died, at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died, at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 太宗舉哀於別次，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: The Emperor held mourning in a separate chamber and wept for him with great grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held mourning in a separate chamber and wept for him with overwhelming grief.

sentences.zh: 賜東園秘器，陪葬昭陵，贈禮部尚書，謚曰文懿。

translations.literal: He was granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, buried with Zhaoling, posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, and given the posthumous title Weny.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, buried at Zhaoling, posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, and given the posthumous title Weny.

sentences.zh: 手敕魏王泰曰：「虞世南於我，猶一體也。

translations.literal: In a personal edict to Prince Wei Tai he said: "Yu Shinan toward me is like one body.
translations.idiomatic: In a personal edict to Prince Wei Tai he said: "Yu Shinan toward me is like one body.

sentences.zh: 拾遺補闕，無日暫忘，實當代名臣，人倫准的。

translations.literal: Rectifying omissions and supplying deficiencies—never a day forgotten. He truly is a famed minister of this age, the measure for human relations.
translations.idiomatic: He rectified omissions and supplied deficiencies without a single day's forgetfulness. He was truly a famed minister of this age and the standard by which human conduct is measured.

sentences.zh: 吾有小失，必犯顏而諫之。

translations.literal: When I have a small fault he always offends my countenance to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I had a small fault, he would offend my countenance to remonstrate with me.

sentences.zh: 今其雲亡，石渠、東觀之中，無復人矣，痛惜豈可言耶！

translations.literal: Now that he has passed like a cloud, in the Stone Canal and Eastern Archive there is no one left. How can the pain be expressed!
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has passed like a cloud, in the Stone Canal and Eastern Archive there is no one left. How can such grief be put into words!

sentences.zh: 」未幾，太宗為詩一篇，追述往古興亡之道，既而嘆曰：「鐘子期死，伯牙不復鼓琴。

translations.literal: " Not long after, the Emperor composed a poem tracing the paths of rise and fall in antiquity, then sighed: "When Zhong Ziqi died, Bo Ya never again played the zither.
translations.idiomatic: " Not long after, the Emperor composed a poem tracing the paths of rise and fall in antiquity, then sighed: "When Zhong Ziqi died, Bo Ya never again played the zither.

sentences.zh: 朕之此詩，將何以示？

translations.literal: For this poem of mine, to whom shall I show it?
translations.idiomatic: For this poem of mine, to whom shall I show it?

sentences.zh: 」令起居郎褚遂良詣其靈帳讀訖焚之，冀世南神識感悟。

translations.literal: " He ordered Attendant for Drafting Chu Suiliang to go to his spirit curtained hall, read it through, and burn it, hoping Shinian's spirit might be moved to awareness.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Attendant for Drafting Chu Suiliang to go to his spirit curtained hall, read it through, and burn it, hoping Shinian's spirit might be moved to awareness.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，太宗夜夢見之，有若平生。

translations.literal: Several years later the Emperor dreamed of him at night as though in life.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the Emperor dreamed of him at night as though he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 翌日，下制曰：「禮部尚書、永興文懿公虞世南，德行淳備，文為辭宗，夙夜盡心，志在忠益。

translations.literal: The next day he issued an edict saying: "Minister of Rites, Duke Weny of Yongxing, Yu Shinan—his virtue and conduct were pure and complete, his writing the master of words, day and night with utmost heart, his aim loyal benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he issued an edict saying: "Minister of Rites, Duke Weny of Yongxing, Yu Shinan—his virtue and conduct were pure and complete, his writing the master of words, day and night with utmost devotion, his aim loyal benefit.

sentences.zh: 奄從物化，倏移歲序，昨因夜夢，忽睹其人，兼進讜言，有如平生之日。

translations.literal: Suddenly he followed things in transformation; years swiftly shift. Yesterday because of a dream at night I suddenly saw him, and moreover he advanced frank words as on the day of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he followed things in transformation, and the years swiftly shifted. Yesterday, because of a dream at night, I suddenly saw him, and moreover he advanced frank words as on the day of his life.

sentences.zh: 追懷遺美，良增悲嘆。

translations.literal: Recalling his remaining beauty, I am much increased in grief and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling his remaining virtues, I am filled with still greater grief and sighing.

sentences.zh: 宜資冥助，申朕思舊之情，可於其家為設五百僧齋，並為造天尊像一區。

translations.literal: He should be assisted in the hidden realm to express my thought of old friendship: at his home let five hundred monk feasts be set up, and also have made one image of the Heavenly Honored One.
translations.idiomatic: He should be assisted in the hidden realm to express my longing for an old friend: at his home let five hundred monk feasts be set up, and also have made one image of the Heavenly Honored One.

sentences.zh: 」又敕圖其形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: " He also ordered his likeness painted in Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered his likeness painted in Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 有集三十捲，令褚亮為之序。

translations.literal: He had a collection of thirty scrolls; Chu Liang was ordered to write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of thirty scrolls, and Chu Liang was ordered to write the preface.

sentences.zh: 世南子昶，官至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shinian's son Chang reached the office of Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shinian's son Chang rose to the office of Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 李百藥，字重規，定州安平人，隋內史令、安平公德林子也。

translations.literal: Li Baiyao, styled Chonggui, was a native of Anping in Dingzhou, son of Li Delin, Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Anping of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baiyao, whose style was Chonggui, came from Anping in Dingzhou. He was the son of Li Delin, Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Anping under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 為童兒時多疾病，祖母趙氏故以百藥為名。

translations.literal: As a child he was often ill; his grandmother the Lady Zhao therefore gave him the name Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was often ill, so his grandmother, Lady Zhao, gave him the name Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 七歲解屬文。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose linked prose.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he could compose linked prose.

sentences.zh: 父友齊中書舍人陸乂、馬元熙嘗造德林宴集，有讀徐陵文者，雲「既取成周之禾，將刈琅邪之稻」，並不知其事。

translations.literal: His father's friends, Qi Attendant of the Secretariat Lu Yi and Ma Yuanxi, once came to Delin's banquet; someone read Xu Ling's prose saying "having taken the grain of accomplished Zhou, about to reap the rice of Langye"—both did not know the matter's source.
translations.idiomatic: His father's friends, Qi Attendant of the Secretariat Lu Yi and Ma Yuanxi, once came to Delin's banquet. Someone read Xu Ling's prose saying "having taken the grain of accomplished Zhou, about to reap the rice of Langye," and neither man knew the allusion.

sentences.zh: 百藥時侍立，進曰：「《傳》稱『鄅人藉稻』。

translations.literal: Baiyao at the time stood in attendance and advanced: "The Zuo zhuan says 'the people of Yun borrowed rice.'
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao, standing in attendance, stepped forward and said: "The Zuo zhuan says, 'the people of Yun borrowed rice.'

sentences.zh: 杜預《注》雲『鄅國在琅邪開陽』。

translations.literal: Du Yu's commentary says 'the state of Yun was in Kaiyang, Langye.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu's commentary says, 'the state of Yun was in Kaiyang, Langye.'

sentences.zh: 」乂等大驚異之。

translations.literal: " Yi and the others were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi and the others were greatly astonished.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，授東宮通事舍人，遷太子舍人，兼東宮學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Emissary Attendant of the Eastern Palace, promoted to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and concurrently Eastern Palace Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Emissary Attendant of the Eastern Palace, promoted to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and concurrently made an Eastern Palace Scholar.

sentences.zh: 或嫉其才而毀之者，乃謝病免去。

translations.literal: Some who envied his talent slandered him, and he therefore resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Some who envied his talent slandered him, and he therefore resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十九年，追赴仁壽宮，令襲父爵。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was summoned to Renshou Palace and ordered to inherit his father's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was summoned to Renshou Palace and ordered to inherit his father's noble rank.

sentences.zh: 左僕射楊素、吏部尚書牛弘雅愛其才，奏授禮部員外郎，皇太子勇又召為東宮學士。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Yang Su and Minister of Civil Office Niu Hong greatly loved his talent and memorialized appointing him Vice Director of Rites; Crown Prince Yong also summoned him as Eastern Palace Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yang Su and Minister of Civil Office Niu Hong greatly admired his talent and memorialized his appointment as Vice Director of Rites. Crown Prince Yong also summoned him as an Eastern Palace Scholar.

sentences.zh: 詔令修五禮，定律令，撰陰陽書。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compile the Five Rites, fix laws and statutes, and compose books on yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the Five Rites, fix laws and statutes, and compose books on yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 台內奏議文表，多百藥所撰。

translations.literal: Memorials, deliberations, documents, and reports within the Secretariat were mostly composed by Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials, deliberations, documents, and reports within the Secretariat were mostly composed by Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝出鎮揚州，嘗召之，百藥辭疾不赴，煬帝大怒，及即位，出為桂州司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang went out to command Yangzhou he once summoned him; Baiyao pleaded illness and did not go. The Emperor was greatly angered, and at enthronement demoted him to Army Commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang went out to command Yangzhou he once summoned him, but Baiyao pleaded illness and did not go. The Emperor was greatly angered, and when he took the throne he demoted Baiyao to Army Commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 為沈法興所得，署為掾。

translations.literal: He was obtained by Shen Faxing and appointed as aide.
translations.idiomatic: He fell into the hands of Shen Faxing and was appointed as his aide.

sentences.zh: 其後，罷州置郡，因解職還鄉里。

translations.literal: Later, when the province was abolished and a prefecture established, he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the province was abolished and a prefecture established in its place, he resigned and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，授魯郡臨泗府步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye he was appointed Infantry Commandant of Linsi Prefecture in Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye he was appointed Infantry Commandant of Linsi Prefecture in Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，充戍會稽。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as garrison soldier at Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he served as a garrison soldier at Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 尋授建安郡丞，行達烏程，屬江都難作，復會沈法興為李子通所破，子通又命為中書侍郎、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Acting Administrator of Jian'an; reaching Wucheng, at Jiangdu the calamity occurred. He again met Shen Faxing, destroyed by Li Zitong, who again appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellor of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Acting Administrator of Jian'an. When he reached Wucheng, the calamity at Jiangdu occurred. He again encountered Shen Faxing, who had been destroyed by Li Zitong; Zitong then appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellor of the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 及杜伏威攻滅子通，又以百藥為行台考功郎中。

translations.literal: When Du Fuwei attacked and destroyed Zitong, he again appointed Baiyao Reviewing Merits Attendant of the Mobile Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Fuwei attacked and destroyed Zitong, he again appointed Baiyao Reviewing Merits Attendant of the Mobile Court.

sentences.zh: 或有譖之者，伏威囚之，百藥著《省躬賦》以致其情，伏威亦知其無罪，乃令復職。

translations.literal: Some slandered him; Fuwei imprisoned him. Baiyao wrote the "Reflection on Self" to express his situation; Fuwei also knew he was guiltless and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Some slandered him, and Fuwei imprisoned him. Baiyao wrote the "Reflection on Self" to express his situation. Fuwei also knew he was guiltless and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 伏威既據有江南，高祖遣使招撫，百藥勸伏威入朝，伏威從之，遣其行台僕射輔公祏與百藥留守，遂詣京師。

translations.literal: When Fuwei held Jiangnan, Gaozu sent envoys to summon and pacify; Baiyao urged Fuwei to enter court. Fuwei followed, sent his Mobile Court Deputy Prime Minister Fu Gongshi with Baiyao to stay and guard, and proceeded to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fuwei held Jiangnan, Gaozu sent envoys to summon and pacify him. Baiyao urged Fuwei to enter court, and Fuwei agreed. He sent his Mobile Court Deputy Prime Minister Fu Gongshi to stay behind with Baiyao as guard, and then proceeded to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及渡江至歷陽，狐疑中悔，將害百藥，乃飲以石灰酒，因大洩痢，而宿病皆除。

translations.literal: When crossing the river to Liyang, hesitating and repenting mid-way, he was about to kill Baiyao and made him drink lime wine; he suffered great dysentery, yet all his chronic illnesses were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: When he crossed the river to Liyang, hesitating and repenting midway, he was about to kill Baiyao and made him drink lime wine. Baiyao suffered severe dysentery, yet all his chronic illnesses were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 伏威知百藥不死，乃作書與公祏令殺百藥，賴伏威養子王雄誕保護獲免。

translations.literal: Fuwei, knowing Baiyao did not die, wrote to Gongshi ordering him to kill Baiyao; relying on Fuwei's adopted son Wang Xiongdan's protection he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei, knowing Baiyao had not died, wrote to Gongshi ordering him to kill Baiyao. Thanks to the protection of Fuwei's adopted son Wang Xiongdan, he escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 公祏反，又授百藥吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gongshi rebelled, he again appointed Baiyao Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi rebelled, he again appointed Baiyao Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 有譖百藥於高祖，雲百藥初說杜伏威入朝，又與輔公祏同反。

translations.literal: Some slandered Baiyao to Gaozu, saying Baiyao first urged Du Fuwei to enter court and also joined Fu Gongshi in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Some slandered Baiyao to Gaozu, saying that Baiyao had first urged Du Fuwei to enter court and had also joined Fu Gongshi in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was greatly enraged.

sentences.zh: 及公祏平，得伏威與公祏令殺百藥書，高祖意稍解，遂配流涇州。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was pacified, Fuwei's letter to Gongshi ordering Baiyao's death was obtained; Gaozu's anger somewhat eased, and he was banished to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi was pacified, Fuwei's letter to Gongshi ordering Baiyao's death was obtained. Gaozu's anger somewhat eased, and Baiyao was banished to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 臣聞經國庇民，王者之常制；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that governing the state and sheltering the people is the constant institution of kings;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that governing the state and sheltering the people is the constant institution of kings;

sentences.zh: 尊主安上，人情之本方。

translations.literal: honoring the lord and securing superiors is the root pattern of human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: honoring the lord and securing superiors is the root pattern of human sentiment.

sentences.zh: 思闡治定之規，以弘長世之業者，萬古不易，百慮同歸。

translations.literal: Those who think to clarify rules for order and stability and extend the enterprise of lasting generations—this is unchanged through ten thousand ages; a hundred schemes share one return.
translations.idiomatic: Those who seek to clarify rules for order and stability and extend the enterprise of lasting generations find that this aim is unchanged through ten thousand ages and that a hundred schemes share one return.

sentences.zh: 然命歷有賒促之殊，邦家有理亂之異，遐觀載籍，論之詳矣。

translations.literal: Yet fate and chronology have differences of short and long; states have differences of order and chaos—gazing distantly at records, this is discussed in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fate and chronology differ in whether they are brief or prolonged, and states differ in whether they are well ordered or chaotic. A distant view of the records discusses this in detail.

sentences.zh: 咸雲周過其數，秦不及期，存亡之理，在於郡國。

translations.literal: All say Zhou exceeded its allotted number, Qin did not reach its term; the principle of survival or extinction lies in commanderies and principalities.
translations.idiomatic: All say that Zhou exceeded its allotted span and Qin did not reach its term; the principle of survival or extinction lies in commanderies and principalities.

sentences.zh: 可以監夏殷之長久，遵黃唐之並建，維城盤石，深根固本，雖王綱弛廢，枝幹相持，故使逆節不生，宗祀不絕。

translations.literal: One may take warning from the longevity of Xia and Yin, follow the Yellow Emperor and Tang in joint establishment; secure walls and bedrock, deep roots and solid foundation—though the royal net slackens and falls, trunk and branches support each other, so rebellious nodes do not arise and ancestral sacrifices are not cut off.
translations.idiomatic: One may take warning from the longevity of Xia and Yin and follow the Yellow Emperor and Tang in joint establishment: secure walls and bedrock, deep roots and a solid foundation. Though the royal net slackens and falls, trunk and branches support each other, so rebellious nodes do not arise and ancestral sacrifices are not cut off.

sentences.zh: 秦氏背師古之訓，棄先王之道，踐華恃險，罷侯置守，子弟無尺土之邑，兆庶罕共治之憂，故一夫號澤，七廟隳祀。

translations.literal: The Qin clan turned from the instructions of teachers of antiquity, abandoned the Way of former kings, trampled on splendor and relied on peril, abolished marquisates and established defenders—sons and younger brothers without territories of a foot, the myriad people rarely with the worry of joint governance; therefore one man shouted in the marshes and the seven temples were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin clan turned from the instructions of teachers of antiquity and abandoned the Way of former kings. It trampled on splendor and relied on peril, abolished marquisates and established defenders. Sons and younger brothers held not even a foot of territory, and the myriad people rarely shared the worry of joint governance. Therefore one man shouted in the marshes and the seven temples were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 臣以為自古皇王，君臨宇內，莫不受命上玄，飛名帝錄，締構遇興王之運，殷憂屬啟聖之期。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that since antiquity emperors and kings ruling within the four seas—none did not receive mandate from the High Mystery, fly their names in the emperor's register; their founding met the fortune of a king who rose, their deep anxiety belonged to the season of a sage who opened.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that since antiquity, emperors and kings who ruled within the four seas all received mandate from the High Mystery and had their names entered in the emperor's register. Their founding met the fortune of a rising king, and their deep anxiety belonged to the season of a sage who opened the age.

sentences.zh: 雖魏武攜養之資，漢高徒役之賤，非止意有覬覦，推之亦不能去也。

translations.literal: Though Cao Wei had the credentials of fostered authority and Han Gaozu was lowly as conscripted laborer—not only if their intent had covetousness could they be pushed away; they also could not depart.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cao Wei had the credentials of fostered authority and Han Gaozu was lowly as a conscripted laborer, it was not only that if their intent had covetousness they could be pushed away; they also could not be made to depart.

sentences.zh: 若其獄訟不歸，菁華已竭，雖帝堯之光被四表，大舜之上齊七政，非止情存揖讓，守之亦不可固焉。

translations.literal: If lawsuits did not return to them and their essential brilliance was exhausted, though Emperor Yao's light covered the four quarters and Great Shun aligned with the seven regulators—not only if affection remained for yielding could they also not be firmly held.
translations.idiomatic: If lawsuits no longer returned to them and their essential brilliance was exhausted, then though Emperor Yao's light covered the four quarters and Great Shun aligned with the seven regulators, it was not only that if affection remained for yielding they could be kept; they also could not be firmly held.

sentences.zh: 以放勳、重華之德，尚不能克昌厥後，是知祚之長短，必在天時，政或盛衰，有關人事。

translations.literal: With the virtue of Emperor Yao and Chonghua they still could not make their posterity flourish—thus one knows the length of a reign must lie in heaven's season; whether government flourishes or declines has to do with human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With the virtue of Emperor Yao and Chonghua they still could not make their posterity flourish. Thus one knows that the length of a reign must lie in heaven's season, and whether government flourishes or declines has to do with human affairs.

sentences.zh: 隆周卜代三十，卜年七百，雖淪胥之道斯極，而文、武之器猶存，斯則龜鼎之祚，已懸定於杳冥也。

translations.literal: Flourishing Zhou divined thirty generations, seven hundred years—though the way of ruin reached its extreme, the vessels of Wen and Wu still survived; thus the tortoise-and-cauldron reign was already suspended fixed in the dark unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Flourishing Zhou divined thirty generations and seven hundred years. Though the way of ruin reached its extreme, the vessels of Wen and Wu still survived. Thus the tortoise-and-cauldron reign was already fixed in the dark unknown.

sentences.zh: 至使南征不返，東遷避逼，禋祀如線，郊畿不守，此乃凌夷之漸，有累於封建焉。

translations.literal: It came to the southern expedition not returning, eastern relocation fleeing pressure, sacrifices like a thread, suburban precincts not defended—this is the gradual slide to ruin, with a bearing on feudal enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: It came to the point that the southern expedition did not return, the eastern relocation fled pressure, sacrifices hung by a thread, and suburban precincts were not defended. This is the gradual slide to ruin, and it bears on feudal enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 暴秦運短閏余，數鐘百六。

translations.literal: Violent Qin's fortune was short in intercalary excess; its count struck a hundred-six.
translations.idiomatic: Violent Qin's fortune was brief in its intercalary excess, and its count struck the hundred-six.

sentences.zh: 受命之主，德異禹、湯；

translations.literal: The ruler who received mandate—his virtue unlike Yu and Tang;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler who received mandate—his virtue was unlike that of Yu and Tang;

sentences.zh: 繼世之君，才非啟、誦。

translations.literal: the succeeding ruler's talent unlike Qi and Song.
translations.idiomatic: the succeeding ruler's talent was unlike that of Qi and Song.

sentences.zh: 借使李斯、王綰之輩，盛開四履，將閭、子嬰之徒，俱啟千乘，豈能逆帝子之勃興，抗龍顏之基命者也！

translations.literal: Even if men like Li Si and Wang Wan widely opened four domains, and like Jiang Lu and Ziying all raised a thousand chariots—how could they reverse the sudden rise of the imperial son, resist the foundation-mandate of the dragon countenance!
translations.idiomatic: Even if men like Li Si and Wang Wan widely opened four domains, and men like Jiang Lu and Ziying all raised a thousand chariots, how could they reverse the sudden rise of the imperial son or resist the foundation-mandate of the dragon countenance!

sentences.zh: 然則得失成敗，各有由焉。

translations.literal: Then gain, loss, success, and failure each have their cause.
translations.idiomatic: Thus gain, loss, success, and failure each have their cause.

sentences.zh: 而著述之家，多守常轍，莫不情亡今古，理蔽澆淳，欲以百王之季，行三代之法。

translations.literal: Yet writers mostly guard constant ruts, invariably forgetting present and past, reason obscured by shallow custom, wishing in the twilight of a hundred kings to practice the laws of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet writers mostly guard constant ruts, invariably forgetting present and past, their reason obscured by shallow custom, wishing in the twilight of a hundred kings to practice the laws of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 天下五服之內，盡封諸侯；

translations.literal: Within the five garments of the realm, entirely enfeoff marquis and lords;
translations.idiomatic: Within the five garments of the realm, they would enfeoff marquis and lords throughout;

sentences.zh: 王畿千乘之間，俱為采地。

translations.literal: within the thousand chariots of the royal domain, all become fief lands.
translations.idiomatic: and within the thousand chariots of the royal domain, all would become fief lands.

sentences.zh: 是以結繩之化，行虞、夏之朝；

translations.literal: Thus the transformation of knotted cords practiced in the courts of Yu and Xia;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the transformation of knotted cords would be practiced in the courts of Yu and Xia;

sentences.zh: 用象刑之典，治劉、曹之末，紀綱既紊，斷可知焉。

translations.literal: using the canon of symbolic punishments to govern the ends of Han and Cao—the warp already tangled, severance may be known.
translations.idiomatic: and the canon of symbolic punishments would be used to govern the ends of Han and Cao. Once the warp is tangled, severance may be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 鍥船求劍，未見其可；

translations.literal: Notching the boat to seek the sword—one does not see that it can work;
translations.idiomatic: Notching the boat to seek the sword—one does not see that it can work;

sentences.zh: 膠柱成文，彌所多惑。

translations.literal: gluing the pillar to make writing—still more places of confusion.
translations.idiomatic: gluing the pillar to make writing—this only multiplies confusion.

sentences.zh: 徒知問鼎請隧，有懼霸王之師；

translations.literal: Only knowing that asking for the tripod and requesting the imperial pathway brings fear of the hegemon's army;
translations.idiomatic: They only know that asking for the tripod and requesting the imperial pathway brings fear of the hegemon's army;

sentences.zh: 白馬素車，無復籓籬之援。

translations.literal: white horses and plain carriages—no longer the fence-screen's aid.
translations.idiomatic: white horses and plain carriages—no longer the fence-screen's aid.

sentences.zh: 不悟望夷之釁，未甚羿、浞之災；

translations.literal: Not awakening that the calamity at Wangyi was not yet as severe as the disasters of Yi and Zhuo;
translations.idiomatic: They do not awaken to the fact that the calamity at Wangyi was not yet as severe as the disasters of Yi and Zhuo;

sentences.zh: 高貴之殃，寧異申、繒之酷！

translations.literal: the disaster of the honored—how does it differ from the cruelty of Shen and Zeng!
translations.idiomatic: the disaster of the honored—how does it differ from the cruelty of Shen and Zeng!

sentences.zh: 乃欽明昏亂，自革安危，固非守宰公侯，以成興廢。

translations.literal: Then Qin and Han muddled dark and bright, themselves changing safety and peril—this is truly not making prefects and nobles succeed in rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qin and Han muddled dark and bright and themselves changed safety and peril. This is truly not a matter of making prefects and nobles succeed in rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 且數世之後，王室浸微，始自籓屏，化為仇敵。

translations.literal: And after several generations the royal house gradually weakened, beginning from the screen of the frontier turning into sworn enemies.
translations.idiomatic: After several generations the royal house gradually weakened, and what began as the screen of the frontier turned into sworn enemies.

sentences.zh: 家殊俗，國異政，強凌弱，眾暴寡，疆場彼此，干戈日尋。

translations.literal: Families differed in custom, states differed in government; the strong bullied the weak, the many ravaged the few; borderlands faced each other, weapons sought each other day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Families differed in custom and states differed in government. The strong bullied the weak and the many ravaged the few. Borderlands faced each other, and weapons were sought day by day.

sentences.zh: 狐駘之役，女子盡髽；

translations.literal: In the campaign at Gulu the women all wore hair of mourning;
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign at Gulu the women all wore mourning hair;

sentences.zh: 崤陵之師，只輪不返。

translations.literal: at the battle of Xiaoling not a single wheel returned.
translations.idiomatic: at the battle of Xiaoling not a single wheel returned.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋略舉一隅，其餘不可勝數。

translations.literal: This merely lifts one corner—the rest cannot be numbered.
translations.idiomatic: This merely lifts one corner; the rest cannot be numbered.

sentences.zh: 陸士衡方規規然云：「嗣王委其九鼎，凶族據其大邑，天下晏然，以治待亂。

translations.literal: Lu Ji was properly saying: "The succeeding king entrusted his nine cauldrons; vicious kindred seized his great cities; all under heaven was tranquil—taking order to await chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji was properly saying: "The succeeding king entrusted his nine cauldrons; vicious kindred seized his great cities; all under heaven was tranquil—taking order to await chaos.

sentences.zh: 」何斯言之謬也！

translations.literal: " How erroneous such words!
translations.idiomatic: " How erroneous such words!

sentences.zh: 而設官分職，任賢使能，以循吏之才，膺共治之寄，刺郡分竹，何代無人？

translations.literal: Yet establishing offices and dividing duties, employing the worthy and using the able, with the talent of an upright official bearing the trust of joint governance—appointing commanderies and dividing bamboo: which age lacked such men?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in establishing offices and dividing duties, employing the worthy and using the able, with the talent of an upright official bearing the trust of joint governance—appointing commanderies and dividing bamboo—which age lacked such men?

sentences.zh: 至使地或呈祥，天不愛寶，民稱父母，政比神明。

translations.literal: It reached the point that the earth presented auspicious signs, heaven did not begrudge treasures, the people called them father and mother, government was compared to spirit illumination.
translations.idiomatic: It reached the point that the earth presented auspicious signs, heaven did not begrudge treasures, the people called them father and mother, and government was compared to spirit illumination.

sentences.zh: 曹元首方區區然稱：「與人共其樂者，人必憂其憂，與人同其安者，人必拯其危。

translations.literal: Cao Shou was crampedly saying: "He who shares his joys with others, others will surely care for his cares; he who shares his security with others, others will surely rescue his peril.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shou was crampedly saying: "He who shares his joys with others, others will surely care for his cares; he who shares his security with others, others will surely rescue his peril.

sentences.zh: 」豈容委以侯伯，則同其安危；

translations.literal: " How could it be permitted to entrust to marquis and earls so they share his safety and peril;
translations.idiomatic: " How could it be permitted to entrust power to marquis and earls so that they share his safety and peril,

sentences.zh: 任之牧宰，則殊其憂樂？

translations.literal: but appoint to prefects and managers so their cares and joys differ?
translations.idiomatic: yet appoint prefects and managers so that their cares and joys differ?

sentences.zh: 何斯言之妄也！

translations.literal: How reckless such words!
translations.idiomatic: How reckless such words!

sentences.zh: 封君列國，藉慶門資，忘其先業之艱難，輕其自然之崇貴，莫不世增淫虐，代益驕侈。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed lords of the states, relying on blessed gate pedigree, forgot the hardship of their ancestors' enterprise, lightly regarded the natural honor of their eminence—none did not generation by generation increase debauchery, dynasty by dynasty add arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed lords of the states, relying on blessed gate pedigree, forgot the hardship of their ancestors' enterprise and lightly regarded the natural honor of their eminence. None failed to increase debauchery generation by generation and add arrogance dynasty by dynasty.

sentences.zh: 自離宮別館，切漢凌雲，或刑人力而將盡，或召諸侯而共樂。

translations.literal: From separate palaces and lodges cutting through to Han's ascending clouds, or exhausting human strength until nearly spent, or summoning the feudal lords to rejoice together.
translations.idiomatic: From separate palaces and lodges rivaling Han's ascending clouds, to exhausting human strength until nearly spent, to summoning the feudal lords to rejoice together.

sentences.zh: 陳靈則君臣悖禮，共侮徵舒；

translations.literal: Duke Ling of Chen then ruler and minister violated ritual, jointly insulting Zheng Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Under Duke Ling of Chen, ruler and minister violated ritual and jointly insulted Zheng Shu;

sentences.zh: 衛宣則父子聚麀，終誅壽、朔。

translations.literal: Duke Xuan of Wei then father and son gathered in incest, finally executing Shou and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: under Duke Xuan of Wei, father and son gathered in incest, finally executing Shou and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 乃雲為己思治，豈若是乎？

translations.literal: Yet they said they thought of governing on their own—could it be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they said they thought of governing on their own—could it be like this?

sentences.zh: 內外群官，選自朝廷，擢士庶以任之，澄水鏡以鑑之，年勞優其階品，考績明其黜陟。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials were selected from the court, promoting scholar-commoners to appoint them, clarifying the water mirror to examine them—years of labor graded their ranks, assessment of achievements clarified demotion and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer officials were selected from the court, scholar-commoners were promoted and appointed, and the water mirror was clarified to examine them. Years of labor graded their ranks, and assessment of achievements clarified demotion and promotion.

sentences.zh: 進取事切，砥礪情深，或俸祿不入私門，妻子不之官舍。

translations.literal: Advance and taking office were urgently practical; sharpening and polishing the feelings deep—some did not let salary enter private gates, wives and children did not go to official quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Advance and taking office were urgently practical, and sharpening and polishing ran deep in feeling. Some did not let salary enter private gates, and wives and children did not go to official quarters.

sentences.zh: 頒條之貴，食不舉火；

translations.literal: The honor of issuing regulations—meals not kindling fire;
translations.idiomatic: Those honored for issuing regulations did not kindle fire for their meals;

sentences.zh: 剖符之重，衣唯補葛。

translations.literal: the weight of splitting talismans—clothes only patched hemp.
translations.idiomatic: those with the weight of splitting talismans wore only patched hemp for clothing.

sentences.zh: 南郡太守，敝布裹身；

translations.literal: the prefect of Nan commandery—worn cloth wrapped his body;
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Nan commandery wrapped himself in worn cloth;

sentences.zh: 萊蕪縣長，凝塵生甑。

translations.literal: the magistrate of Laiwu—congealed dust grew on the cooking pot.
translations.idiomatic: the magistrate of Laiwu had dust so thick on his cooking pot that it looked as though it had never been used.

sentences.zh: 專雲為利圖物，何其爽歟！

translations.literal: to speak only of profit and scheme for things—how misleading!
translations.idiomatic: To speak only of profit and to scheme for gain—how misleading!

sentences.zh: 總而言之，爵非世及，用賢之路斯廣；

translations.literal: summarizing in general, nobility is not hereditary, the path for employing the worthy is thus broadened;
translations.idiomatic: In summary, when nobility is not hereditary, the path for employing the worthy is broadened;

sentences.zh: 民無定主，附下之情不固。

translations.literal: the people have no fixed lord, attachment to subordinates is not firm.
translations.idiomatic: the people have no fixed lord, and their attachment to subordinates is not firm.

sentences.zh: 此乃愚智所辨，安可惑哉！

translations.literal: this is what the foolish and the wise distinguish—how can one be deceived!
translations.idiomatic: This is what the foolish and the wise can tell apart—how can anyone be misled!

sentences.zh: 至如滅國弒君，亂常幹紀，春秋二百年間，略無寧歲。

translations.literal: as for destroying states and regicide, violating norms and subverting rule—in the two hundred years of the Spring and Autumn period, there were hardly any peaceful years.
translations.idiomatic: As for destroying states and murdering rulers, violating norms and subverting the laws—in the two hundred years of the Spring and Autumn period, there were scarcely any peaceful years.

sentences.zh: 次睢咸秩，遂用玉帛之名；

translations.literal: ranked at Sui, all held proper order, then used the names of jade and silk;
translations.idiomatic: At Sui all took their proper ranks and then invoked the formal names of jade and silk;

sentences.zh: 魯道有蕩，每等衣裳之會。

translations.literal: on the road in Lu there was debauchery, every sort of meeting of robes and garments.
translations.idiomatic: On the roads of Lu there was debauchery, and every sort of ceremonial meeting of robes and garments.

sentences.zh: 縱使西漢哀、平之際，東洛桓、靈之時，下吏淫暴，必不至此。

translations.literal: even at the end of Western Han under Ai and Ping, in Eastern Luo under Huan and Ling, debauched and violent lower officials would not have gone this far.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the end of Western Han under Emperors Ai and Ping, or in Eastern Luoyang under Emperors Huan and Ling, debauched and violent lower officials would never have gone this far.

sentences.zh: 為政之理，可一言以蔽之。

translations.literal: the principle of governing can be summed up in a single phrase.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of governance can be summed up in a single phrase.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下握紀御天，膺期啟聖，救億兆之焚溺，掃氛昆於寰區。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty grasps the calendar and governs heaven, accepts the destined period and opens sagely rule, saves hundreds of millions from burning and drowning, and sweeps evil vapors from the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty grasps the calendar and governs heaven, has accepted the destined age and opened sagely rule, rescued the hundred million masses from fire and flood, and swept evil vapors from the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 創業垂統，配二儀以立德；

translations.literal: founding enterprise and handing down succession, matching the Two Principles to establish virtue;
