translations.idiomatic: You have founded the enterprise and handed down the succession, matching heaven and earth in establishing virtue;

sentences.zh: 發號施令，妙萬物而為言。

translations.literal: issuing commands and promulgating orders, speaking with the wondrousness of the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: in issuing commands and promulgating orders, you speak with the wondrousness of the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 獨照宸衷，永懷前古，將復五等而修舊制，建萬國以親諸侯。

translations.literal: Your Majesty alone illuminates the imperial heart, forever cherishing antiquity, intending to restore the five ranks and repair the old system, establishing myriad states to draw close the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty alone illuminates the imperial heart and forever cherishes antiquity, intending to restore the five ranks and repair the old system and to establish myriad states to draw the feudal lords close.

sentences.zh: 竊以漢、魏以還，餘風之弊未盡；

translations.literal: I venture to say that since Han and Wei, the defects of residual customs have not been exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that since Han and Wei, the defects of residual customs have not yet been exhausted;

sentences.zh: 勳、華既往，至公之道斯革。

translations.literal: merit and glory have passed away, the way of utmost fairness is thus changed.
translations.idiomatic: merit and glory have passed away, and the way of utmost fairness has been altered.

sentences.zh: 況晉氏失馭，宇縣崩離；

translations.literal: moreover the Jin house lost control, the realm collapsed and split apart;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Jin house lost control and the realm collapsed and split apart;

sentences.zh: 後魏時乘，華夷雜處。

translations.literal: Later Wei took advantage of the times, Chinese and barbarians mixed together.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei took advantage of the times, and Chinese and barbarians lived mixed together.

sentences.zh: 重以關河分阻，吳、楚懸隔，習文者學長短縱橫之術，習武者盡干戈戰爭之心，畢為狙詐之階，彌長澆浮之俗。

translations.literal: Compounded by the Pass and River dividing barriers, Wu and Chu far apart, those studying letters learned the arts of short and long and vertical and horizontal alliance, those studying martial arts filled with the mind of weapons and war—all became steps to cunning trickery, ever lengthening shallow and floating customs.
translations.idiomatic: Compounded by the barrier of the passes and rivers, with Wu and Chu far apart, those who studied letters learned the arts of short and long alliance and vertical and horizontal diplomacy, while those who studied martial arts were filled with the mind of weapons and war. All this became a ladder to cunning trickery and ever lengthened shallow and floating customs.

sentences.zh: 開皇在運，因藉外家。

translations.literal: Kaihuang had fortune in his favor, relying on his maternal relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui had fortune on his side and relied on his maternal relatives.

sentences.zh: 驅御群英，任雄猜之數；

translations.literal: driving and controlling the multitude of heroes, trusting in the method of bold suspicion;
translations.idiomatic: He drove and controlled the multitude of heroes and trusted in the method of bold suspicion;

sentences.zh: 坐移時運，非克定之功。

translations.literal: he sat and shifted with the turning of fortune, not the achievement of pacifying through conquest.
translations.idiomatic: he merely shifted with the turning of fortune and did not achieve true pacification through conquest.

sentences.zh: 年逾二紀，民不見德。

translations.literal: more than twenty years passed, the people did not see virtue.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty years passed, and the people did not see virtue.

sentences.zh: 及大業嗣文，世道交喪，一時人物，掃地將盡。

translations.literal: when Daye succeeded Wen, the ways of the world were mutually lost, the men of the age were nearly swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded Emperor Wen, the ways of the world were lost together, and the outstanding men of the age were nearly swept away.

sentences.zh: 雖天縱神武，削平寇虐，兵威不息，勞止未康。

translations.literal: although heaven endowed divine martial prowess, quelling rebel cruelty, military might did not cease, labor and rest were not yet at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Although heaven endowed Your Majesty with divine martial prowess and you quelled rebel cruelty, military might has not ceased and labor and rest are not yet secure.

sentences.zh: 自陛下仰順聖慈，嗣膺寶歷，情深致治，綜核前王。

translations.literal: since Your Majesty looked up and followed the sage compassion, succeeded to the imperial calendar, deep in feeling pursued good governance, examining and verifying former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty looked up and followed the sage compassion, succeeded to the imperial throne, pursued good governance with deep feeling, and examined and verified the ways of former kings,

sentences.zh: 雖至道無名，言象所紀，略陳梗概，實所庶幾。

translations.literal: although the ultimate Way is nameless, what words and images record—a brief outline is truly what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: although the ultimate Way is nameless and only words and images can record it, I offer a brief outline of what I truly hope for.

sentences.zh: 愛敬蒸蒸，勞而不倦，大舜之孝也。

translations.literal: love and reverence rising warmly, laboring without weariness—this is the filial piety of Great Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Your love and reverence rise warmly, and you labor without weariness—this is the filial piety of Great Shun.

sentences.zh: 訪安內豎，親嘗御膳，文王之德也。

translations.literal: inquiring after the comfort of inner attendants, personally tasting the imperial meals—this is the virtue of King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: You inquire after the comfort of inner attendants and personally taste the imperial meals—this is the virtue of King Wen.

sentences.zh: 每憲司讞罪，尚書奏獄，大小必察，枉直咸申，舉斷趾之法，易大辟之刑，仁心隱惻，貫徹幽顯，大禹之泣辜也。

translations.literal: whenever the censorate reviewed crimes and the Secretariat reported on prisons, great and small were always examined, wrong and right both upheld, abolishing the punishment of cutting off feet, replacing capital punishment—benevolent heart deeply compassionate, penetrating hidden and manifest—this is Yu the Great weeping for the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the censorate reviews crimes and the Secretariat reports on prisons, you examine great and small cases alike and uphold both the wronged and the upright. You have abolished the punishment of cutting off the feet and replaced capital punishment. Your benevolent heart is deeply compassionate and reaches both the hidden and the manifest—this is Yu the Great weeping for the guilty.

sentences.zh: 正色直言，虛心受納，不簡鄙陋，無棄芻蕘，帝堯之求諫也。

translations.literal: with stern countenance speaking straight, with empty heart receiving and accepting, not disdaining the lowly and crude, not discarding fodder and firewood gatherers—this is Emperor Yao seeking remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: You speak with stern countenance and straight words, receive advice with an open heart, do not disdain the lowly and crude, and do not discard humble commoners—this is Emperor Yao seeking remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 弘獎名教，勸勵學徒，既擢明經於青紫，將升碩儒於卿相，聖人之善誘也。

translations.literal: expanding and rewarding name and teaching, encouraging and urging students, already selecting those who mastered the classics for blue and purple, about to promote great scholars to ministers and chancellors—this is the sage's good guidance.
translations.idiomatic: You expand and reward name and teaching and encourage students. You have already selected those who mastered the classics for blue and purple robes and are about to promote great scholars to ministers and chancellors—this is the sage's good guidance.

sentences.zh: 群臣以宮中暑濕，寢膳或乖，請徙御高明，營一小閣。

translations.literal: the ministers, because the palace was hot and damp, sleep and meals sometimes improper, requested moving the imperial residence to a high bright place, building a small pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Because the palace was hot and damp and sleep and meals were sometimes improper, the ministers requested that the imperial residence be moved to a high bright place and a small pavilion be built.

sentences.zh: 遂惜家人之產，竟抑子來之願，不吝陰陽所感，以安卑陋之居。

translations.literal: then cherishing the family's resources, finally suppressing the people's willing coming, not sparing what yin and yang affect, to dwell in humble low quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you cherished the resources of the people, suppressed their willing labor, and did not spare what yin and yang might affect, choosing instead to dwell in humble quarters.

sentences.zh: 去歲荒儉，普天饑饉，喪亂甫爾，倉廩空虛。

translations.literal: last year there was famine and scarcity, heaven-wide hunger, the disorders had just ceased, granaries empty.
translations.idiomatic: Last year there was famine and scarcity, hunger throughout the realm, the disorders had only just ended, and the granaries were empty.

sentences.zh: 聖情矜愍，勤加惠恤，竟無一人流離道路，猶且食啖藜藿，樂撤簨弶，言必淒動，貌成癯瘠。

translations.literal: the sage feeling pity and compassion, diligently adding kindness and relief—still not a single person wandering on the roads, yet still eating wild greens, gladly removing the meat from meals, words always moving with sorrow, appearance becoming wasted and lean.
translations.idiomatic: Your sage feeling was full of pity and compassion, and you diligently added kindness and relief until not a single person wandered on the roads. Yet you still ate wild greens, gladly removed meat from your meals, spoke always with moving sorrow, and your appearance became wasted and lean.

sentences.zh: 公旦喜於重譯，文命矜其即序。

translations.literal: the Duke of Zhou rejoiced at repeated translation, Wen Ming took pity on those coming into order.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou rejoiced when foreign envoys came again and again through interpreters, and Yu the Great took pity on those who came into order.

sentences.zh: 陛下每四夷款附，萬里歸仁，必退思進省。

translations.literal: Your Majesty whenever the four barbarians sincerely submitted, from ten thousand miles returning to benevolence, always withdrew to reflect and advance in self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the four barbarians sincerely submitted and returned to benevolence from ten thousand miles away, Your Majesty always withdrew to reflect and examine yourself.

sentences.zh: 凝神動慮，恐妄勞中國，以事遠方，不藉萬古之英聲，以存一時之茂實。

translations.literal: concentrating spirit and moving thought, fearing recklessly exhausting China for distant affairs, not borrowing ten-thousand-year heroic fame to preserve momentary abundant reality.
translations.idiomatic: You concentrate your spirit and turn your thoughts, fearing to exhaust China recklessly for distant affairs and refusing to borrow ten-thousand-year heroic fame in order to preserve momentary abundance.

sentences.zh: 心切憂勞，跡絕游幸，每旦視朝，聽受無倦。

translations.literal: heart deeply anxious and toiling, traces cut off from pleasure tours, every dawn attending court, listening without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Your heart is deeply anxious and toiling, your traces have ceased from pleasure tours, and every dawn you attend court and listen without weariness.

sentences.zh: 智周於萬物，道濟於天下。

translations.literal: wisdom encompassing the myriad things, the Way benefiting the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your wisdom encompasses the myriad things, and your Way benefits the realm.

sentences.zh: 罷朝之後，引進名臣，討論是非，備盡肝膈，唯及政事，更無異辭。

translations.literal: after court dismissal, summoning famous ministers, discussing right and wrong, fully exposing innermost hearts, only touching on governance—nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: After court is dismissed, you summon famous ministers, discuss right and wrong, and fully expose your innermost thoughts, touching only on governance and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 才及日昃，命才學之士，賜以清閒，高談典籍，雜以文詠，間以玄言，乙夜忘疲，中宵不寐。

translations.literal: just as the sun reached west, ordering men of talent and learning, granting them leisure, discussing classics at length, mixed with literary verse, interspersed with profound discourse—forgetting fatigue into the second watch of night, not sleeping at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the sun reaches the west, you summon men of talent and learning, grant them leisure, discuss the classics at length, mix in literary verse, and intersperse profound discourse, forgetting fatigue into the second watch of the night and not sleeping at midnight.

sentences.zh: 此之四道，獨邁往初。

translations.literal: these four ways alone surpass all former beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: In these four ways you alone surpass all former beginnings.

sentences.zh: 斯實生民以來，一人而已。

translations.literal: this truly since the birth of the people, one person alone.
translations.idiomatic: Truly since the birth of the people, there has been only one such person.

sentences.zh: 弘茲風化，昭示四方，信可以期月之間，彌綸天壤。

translations.literal: expanding this transformation and teaching, displaying to the four directions—truly within a month or so could spread across heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: If you expand this transformation and teaching and display it to the four directions, it truly could within a month spread across heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 而淳粹尚阻，浮詭未移，此由習之永久，難以卒變。

translations.literal: yet pure simplicity is still blocked, shallow trickery not yet moved—this is because customs are long-standing, hard to change abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pure simplicity is still blocked and shallow trickery has not yet shifted, because customs are long-standing and hard to change all at once.

sentences.zh: 請待斫雕成朴，以質代文，刑措之教一行，登封之禮雲畢，然後定疆理之制，議山河之賞，未為晚焉。

translations.literal: please wait until carving is hewn to plainness, substance replacing ornament, the teaching of punishments set aside once enacted, the Mount Tai ceremony completed—then fix the system of territory and boundaries, discuss rewards of mountains and rivers—not too late.
translations.idiomatic: Please wait until ornament is hewn back to plainness and substance replaces refinement, until the teaching of punishments set aside is fully enacted and the Mount Tai ceremony is completed, and only then fix the system of territory and boundaries and discuss rewards of mountains and rivers—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱：「天地盈虛，與時消息，況於人乎？

translations.literal: The Classic of Changes says: "Heaven and earth wax and wane, advancing and retreating with the times—how much more for people?
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Changes says: "Heaven and earth wax and wane, advancing and retreating with the times—how much more is this true of people?

sentences.zh: 」美哉斯言也。

translations.literal: " How beautiful these words!
translations.idiomatic: " How beautiful these words are!

sentences.zh: 太宗竟從其議。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong finally followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong finally followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 四年，授太子右庶子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Right Subordinate to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was appointed Right Subordinate to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 五年，與左庶子於志寧、中允孔穎達、舍人陸敦信侍講於弘教殿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Left Subordinate Yu Zhining, Palace Secretary Kong Yingda, and Attendant Lu Dunxin, he lectured at Hongjiao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, together with Left Subordinate Yu Zhining, Palace Secretary Kong Yingda, and Attendant Lu Dunxin, he lectured at Hongjiao Hall.

sentences.zh: 時太子頗留意典墳，然閒燕之後，嬉戲過度，百藥作《讚道賦》以諷焉，辭多不載。

translations.literal: At the time the Crown Prince paid considerable attention to the classics, yet after leisure banquets, play exceeded bounds. Baiyao wrote "Ode Praising the Way" to admonish him—the text mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Crown Prince paid considerable attention to the classics, yet after leisure banquets his play exceeded all bounds. Baiyao wrote the "Ode Praising the Way" to admonish him, but most of the text is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 太宗見而遣使謂百藥曰：「朕於皇太子處見卿所獻賦，悉述古來儲貳事以誡太子，甚是典要。

translations.literal: Taizong saw it and sent an envoy to tell Baiyao: "I saw at the Crown Prince's the ode you submitted, entirely recounting ancient affairs of the heir to admonish the Crown Prince—very canonical and essential.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong saw it and sent an envoy to tell Baiyao: "I saw at the Crown Prince's the ode you submitted, which entirely recounts ancient affairs of the heir apparent in order to admonish the Crown Prince. It is very canonical and essential.

sentences.zh: 朕選卿以輔弼太子，正為此事，大稱所委，但須善始令終耳。

translations.literal: I selected you to assist the Crown Prince precisely for this matter—greatly fitting the trust, but you must have a good beginning and a good end.
translations.idiomatic: I selected you to assist the Crown Prince precisely for this matter, and you have greatly fulfilled the trust—but you must have a good beginning and a good end.

sentences.zh: 」因賜彩物五百段。

translations.literal: " And so he bestowed five hundred bolts of colored goods.
translations.idiomatic: " He then bestowed five hundred bolts of colored goods.

sentences.zh: 然太子卒不悟而廢。

translations.literal: Yet the Crown Prince in the end did not awaken and was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Crown Prince in the end did not awaken and was deposed.

sentences.zh: 十年，以撰《齊史》成，加散騎常侍，行太子左庶子，賜物四百段。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, on completion of compiling the History of Qi, he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Cavalry in Attendance, Acting Left Subordinate to the Crown Prince, and granted four hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, on completion of compiling the History of Qi, he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Cavalry in Attendance and Acting Left Subordinate to the Crown Prince, and was granted four hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 俄除宗正卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以撰《五禮》及律令成，進爵為子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on completion of compiling the Five Rites and statutes, he was advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, on completion of compiling the Five Rites and statutes, he was advanced in rank to Viscount.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，以年老固請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: Several years later, on account of old age he firmly requested retirement—this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, on account of old age he firmly requested retirement, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗制《帝京篇》，命百藥並作，上嘆其工，手詔曰：「卿何身之老而才之壯，何齒之宿而意之新乎！

translations.literal: Taizong once composed "Imperial Capital Poems," ordered Baiyao to compose as well. The Emperor admired his skill and wrote in his own hand: "How is your body old yet your talent vigorous, your teeth aged yet your thought fresh!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once composed the "Imperial Capital Poems" and ordered Baiyao to compose as well. The Emperor admired his skill and wrote in his own hand: "How is your body old yet your talent vigorous, your teeth aged yet your thought fresh!

sentences.zh: 」二十二年卒，年八十四，謚曰康。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-second year he died, age eighty-four, posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-second year he died, at the age of eighty-four. His posthumous title was Kang.

sentences.zh: 百藥以名臣之子，才行相繼，四海名流，莫不宗仰。

translations.literal: Baiyao as son of a famous minister, talent and conduct continuing in succession, famous men throughout the realm—none did not honor and look up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was the son of a famous minister, and his talent and conduct continued in succession. Famous men throughout the realm all honored and looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 藻思沈鬱，尤長於五言詩，雖樵童牧豎，並皆吟諷。

translations.literal: Literary thought deep and rich, especially skilled in five-character poetry—even woodcutters and shepherd boys all recited and sang them.
translations.idiomatic: His literary thought was deep and rich, and he was especially skilled in five-character poetry. Even woodcutters and shepherd boys all recited and sang his poems.

sentences.zh: 性好引進後生，提獎不倦。

translations.literal: By nature fond of promoting the young, encouraging without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was fond of promoting the young and encouraging them without weariness.

sentences.zh: 所得俸祿，多散之親黨。

translations.literal: Salary received was mostly distributed to relatives and associates.
translations.idiomatic: The salary he received he mostly distributed among relatives and associates.

sentences.zh: 又至性過人，初侍父母喪還鄉，徒跣單衣，行數千里，服闋數年，容貌毀悴，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Also exceptional filial nature surpassing others—initially attending his parents' funeral and returning home, barefoot in single garment, traveling several thousand li; mourning period ended several years later, appearance wasted and haggard—praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also had an exceptional filial nature that surpassed others. When he first attended his parents' funeral and returned home, he went barefoot in a single garment and traveled several thousand li. Several years after his mourning ended, his appearance was still wasted and haggard, and people of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 及懸車告老，怡然自得，穿池築山，文酒談賞，以舒平生之志。

translations.literal: When hanging up the cart and announcing old age, content and at ease, digging ponds and building hills, literary wine and conversational appreciation—to express lifelong aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: When he hung up his cart and announced his retirement, he was content and at ease, digging ponds and building hills, enjoying literary wine and conversation, in order to express his lifelong aspirations.

sentences.zh: 有集三十捲，子安期。

translations.literal: He had a collection of thirty scrolls; his son was Anqi.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection of thirty scrolls. His son was Anqi.

sentences.zh: 安期幼聰辯，七歲解屬文。

translations.literal: Anqi as a child was clever and eloquent; at seven he could compose linked prose.
translations.idiomatic: Anqi was clever and eloquent as a child, and at seven he could compose linked prose.

sentences.zh: 初，百藥大業末出為桂州司馬，行至太湖，遇逆賊，將加白刃，安期跪泣請代父命，賊哀而釋之。

translations.literal: Initially, Baiyao at the end of Daye went out as Military Assistant of Guizhou; reaching Tai Lake, he encountered rebels and was about to apply the blade. Anqi knelt weeping and begged to die in his father's place—the rebels were moved and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, at the end of the Daye reign Baiyao went out as Military Assistant of Guizhou. When he reached Tai Lake he encountered rebels who were about to kill him. Anqi knelt weeping and begged to die in his father's place, and the rebels were moved and released them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累轉符璽郎。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, he was repeatedly transferred to Keeper of the Seals.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was repeatedly transferred to Keeper of the Seals.

sentences.zh: 預修《晉書》成，除主客員外郎。

translations.literal: On completion of participating in compiling the History of Jin, he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: When his participation in compiling the History of Jin was completed, he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Yonghui, he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又與李義府等於武德殿內修書，再轉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Also with Li Yifu and others he compiled books inside Wude Hall, and was twice transferred to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled books inside Wude Hall with Li Yifu and others, and was twice transferred to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，為司列少常伯，參知軍國。

translations.literal: During Longshuo, he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel, participating in state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longshuo reign he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel and participated in state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 有事太山，詔安期為朝覲壇碑文。

translations.literal: When offering sacrifice at Mount Tai, Anqi was ordered to compose the inscription for the Court Audience Altar.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was offered at Mount Tai, Anqi was ordered to compose the inscription for the Court Audience Altar.

sentences.zh: 安期前後三為選部，頗為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Anqi three times served as head of the Selection Bureau, much praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Anqi served three times as head of the Selection Bureau and was much praised by people of the time.

sentences.zh: 時高宗屢引侍臣，責以不進賢良。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozong repeatedly summoned attendant ministers, reproaching them for not advancing worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Gaozong repeatedly summoned attendant ministers and reproached them for not advancing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 眾皆莫對，獨安期進曰：「臣聞聖帝明王，莫不勞於求賢，逸於任使。

translations.literal: All were silent; only Anqi stepped forward saying: "I have heard that sage emperors and enlightened kings all labor at seeking the worthy and are at ease in employment.
translations.idiomatic: All were silent. Only Anqi stepped forward and said: "I have heard that sage emperors and enlightened kings all labor at seeking the worthy and are at ease in employing them.

sentences.zh: 設使堯、舜苦己癯瘠，不能用賢，終亦王化不行。

translations.literal: Even if Yao and Shun exhausted themselves to emaciation but could not employ the worthy, in the end royal transformation would not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yao and Shun exhausted themselves to emaciation but could not employ the worthy, in the end royal transformation would not proceed.

sentences.zh: 自夏、殷已來，歷國數十，皆委賢良，以共致理。

translations.literal: Since Xia and Yin, passing through dozens of states, all entrusted the worthy to jointly achieve good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xia and Yin, passing through dozens of states, all have entrusted the worthy to achieve good governance together.

sentences.zh: 且十室之邑，必有忠信，況今天下至廣，非無英彥。

translations.literal: Moreover in a hamlet of ten households there must be loyalty and trust—how much more today when the realm is vast, there are not lacking outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in a hamlet of ten households there must be loyalty and trust—how much more today, when the realm is vast and outstanding men are not lacking.

sentences.zh: 但比來公卿有所薦引，即遭囂謗，以為朋黨。

translations.literal: But recently when dukes and ministers made recommendations, they immediately faced clamor and slander, being deemed factional cliques.
translations.idiomatic: But recently when dukes and ministers made recommendations, they immediately faced clamor and slander and were deemed factional cliques.

sentences.zh: 沉屈者未申，而在位者已損，所以人思苟免，競為緘默。

translations.literal: Those sunk and wronged were not vindicated, while those in office were already harmed—therefore people thought of avoiding trouble and competed in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Those sunk and wronged were not vindicated, while those in office were already harmed. Therefore people thought only of avoiding trouble and competed in silence.

sentences.zh: 若陛下虛己招納，務於搜訪，不忌親讎，唯能是用，讒毀亦既不入，誰敢不竭忠誠？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty emptied yourself to recruit and accept, devoted to search and inquiry, not avoiding personal enemies, employing only by ability—slander would not enter either, who would dare not exhaust loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty emptied yourself to recruit and accept, devoted yourself to search and inquiry, did not avoid personal enemies, and employed men only by ability, slander would not enter either. Who would dare not exhaust their loyalty?

sentences.zh: 此皆事由陛下，非臣等所能致也。

translations.literal: All this depends on Your Majesty—it is not what we ministers can bring about.
translations.idiomatic: All this depends on Your Majesty—it is not something we ministers can bring about.

sentences.zh: 」高宗深然其言。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozong deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozong deeply approved his words.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校東台侍郎、同東西台三品，出為荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Eastern Secretariat, Same Rank as the Three Grades of the Eastern and Western Secretariats, and went out as Chief Administrator of the Grand General's Office of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Eastern Secretariat with the same rank as the Three Grades of the Eastern and Western Secretariats, and went out as Chief Administrator of the Grand General's Office of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初卒。

translations.literal: Early in Xianheng he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xianheng reign.

sentences.zh: 自德林至安期三世，皆掌制誥。

translations.literal: From Delin to Anqi for three generations, all held charge of imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: From Delin to Anqi for three generations, all held charge of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 安期孫羲仲，又為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Anqi's grandson Xizhong also served as Secretariat Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Anqi's grandson Xizhong also served as Secretariat Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 褚亮，字希明，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chu Liang, styled Ximing, was a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Liang, whose style was Ximing, came from Qiantang in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖湮，梁御史中丞；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yan was Censor-in-Chief of the Liang;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yan had served as Censor-in-Chief under the Liang;

sentences.zh: 祖蒙，太子中舍人；

translations.literal: his grandfather Meng was Secretariat Aide to the Crown Prince;
translations.idiomatic: his grandfather Meng had been Secretariat Aide to the Crown Prince;

sentences.zh: 父玠，陳秘書監，並著名前史。

translations.literal: his father Jie was Director of the Palace Library under Chen—all noted in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: his father Jie had been Director of the Palace Library under Chen. All were noted in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 其先自陽翟徙居焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors moved from Yangdi and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had moved from Yangdi and settled there.

sentences.zh: 亮幼聰敏好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: As a youth Liang was intelligent and quick-witted, loved learning, and was skilled at composing literary works.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Liang was bright and eager to learn, and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 博覽無所不至，經目必記於心。

translations.literal: He read broadly without limit, and whatever passed before his eyes he always fixed in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely across every field, and whatever he read he committed to memory.

sentences.zh: 喜游名賢，尤善談論。

translations.literal: He delighted in visiting celebrated worthies and was especially adept at debate and discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to seek out eminent men of talent and was especially skilled at discussion and debate.

sentences.zh: 年十八，詣陳僕射徐陵，陵與商榷文章，深異之。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he went to see Chen Vice Director Xu Ling; Ling discussed literary works with him and was deeply impressed.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he visited Xu Ling, Vice Director under Chen, who debated literary matters with him and was greatly struck by his ability.

sentences.zh: 陳後主聞而召見，使賦詩，江總及諸辭人在坐，莫不推善。

translations.literal: When Chen's Last Ruler heard of this he summoned him for an audience, had him compose a poem, and with Jiang Zong and the various writers present, none failed to praise his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Houzhu of Chen heard of him, he summoned Liang to court and asked him to compose a poem. Jiang Zong and the other literary men in attendance all praised his work.

sentences.zh: 禎明初，為尚書殿中侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenming reign he served as Secretariat Attendant within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenming reign he was appointed Secretariat Attendant within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，入隋為東宮學士。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he entered the Sui and served as a Crown Prince Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Chen, he entered Sui service as an academician in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 大業中，授太常博士。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he was made an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝將改置宗廟，亮奏議曰：

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yang was about to reorganize the ancestral temple, and Liang submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yang was planning to reorganize the imperial ancestral temple. Liang submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮記》：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the Book of Rites: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples—the three zhao, the three mu, together with the temple of the Grand Ancestor, making seven.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Book of Rites: "The Son of Heaven maintains seven temples—three zhao, three mu, and the temple of the Grand Ancestor, for a total of seven.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄《注》曰：「此周制也。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan's Commentary says: "This is the Zhou system.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "This refers to the Zhou system.

sentences.zh: 七者，太祖及文王、武王之祧，與親廟四也。

translations.literal: The seven are the Grand Ancestor and the distant shrines of King Wen and King Wu, together with four temples to close ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The seven consist of the Grand Ancestor, the distant shrines of Kings Wen and Wu, and four temples to direct ancestors.

sentences.zh: 殷則六廟，契及湯與二昭二穆也。

translations.literal: The Yin had six temples—Qi and Tang together with two zhao and two mu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin dynasty had six temples: Qi and Tang, plus two zhao and two mu.

sentences.zh: 夏則五廟，無太祖，禹與二昭二穆而已。

translations.literal: The Xia had five temples; there was no Grand Ancestor—only Yu together with two zhao and two mu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia had five temples, with no Grand Ancestor—only Yu and two zhao and two mu.

sentences.zh: 」玄又據《禮》：「王者禘其祖之所自出而立四廟。

translations.literal: " Xuan again cites the Rites: "The king, in the great di sacrifice to the ancestor from whom he traces descent, establishes four temples.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan further cites the Rites: "When the king performs the great di sacrifice to the remote ancestor from whom he traces his line, he establishes four ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 」案鄭玄義，天子唯立四親廟，並始祖而為五。

translations.literal: " Examining Zheng Xuan's interpretation, the Son of Heaven establishes only four temples to close ancestors, together with the Founding Ancestor making five.
translations.idiomatic: " According to Zheng Xuan's interpretation, the Son of Heaven establishes only four temples to direct ancestors, which together with the Founding Ancestor make five.

sentences.zh: 周以文、武為受命之祖，特立二祧，是為七廟。

translations.literal: The Zhou, taking Wen and Wu as the ancestors through whom they received the Mandate, specially established two distant shrines, making seven temples in all.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Zhou regarded Kings Wen and Wu as the founders through whom they received the Mandate, they additionally established two distant shrines, making seven temples in all.

sentences.zh: 王肅注《禮記》曰：「尊者尊統上，卑者尊統下。

translations.literal: Wang Su's commentary on the Book of Rites says: "The exalted honor the line above; the lowly honor the line below.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su's commentary on the Book of Rites states: "Those of high rank honor the line above; those of low rank honor the line below.

sentences.zh: 故天子七廟，諸侯五廟。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five temples.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Son of Heaven maintains seven temples, and feudal lords five.

sentences.zh: 其有殊功異德，非太祖而不毀，不在七廟之數。

translations.literal: Those possessing exceptional merit and virtue, who are not the Grand Ancestor yet whose temples are not destroyed, are not counted within the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors of exceptional merit and virtue whose temples are never abolished—apart from the Grand Ancestor—are not counted among the seven.

sentences.zh: 」案肅以為天子七廟，是百代之言。

translations.literal: " Examining Su's view, the Son of Heaven's seven temples are a principle for all ages.
translations.idiomatic: " Su held that the Son of Heaven's seven temples represent a norm valid for all generations.

sentences.zh: 又據《王制》天子七廟，諸侯五廟，大夫三廟，降二為差。

translations.literal: He further cites the Royal Regulations: the Son of Heaven seven temples, feudal lords five, grand masters three—descending by twos in gradation.
translations.idiomatic: He further cites the Royal Regulations: the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five, grand masters three—a reduction of two at each rank.

sentences.zh: 是則天子立四親廟，又立高祖之父、高祖之祖父、太祖而為七。

translations.literal: Thus the Son of Heaven establishes four temples to close ancestors, and additionally establishes the High Ancestor's father, the High Ancestor's grandfather, and the Grand Ancestor, making seven.
translations.idiomatic: On this view the Son of Heaven establishes four temples to direct ancestors, then adds temples to the High Ancestor's father, the High Ancestor's grandfather, and the Grand Ancestor, for a total of seven.

sentences.zh: 周有文、武、姜嫄合為十廟。

translations.literal: The Zhou had Wen, Wu, and Jiang Yuan, making ten temples in total.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou, with Wen, Wu, and Jiang Yuan added, the total came to ten temples.

sentences.zh: 漢世諸帝之廟各立，無迭毀之義。

translations.literal: In the Han, each emperor's temple was established separately, with no principle of successive destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, each emperor had his own separate temple, with no practice of successive abolition.

sentences.zh: 至元帝時，貢禹、匡衡之徒始議其禮，以高帝為太祖，而立四親，是為五廟。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Yuan, Gong Yu, Kuang Heng, and others first debated this ritual, taking Emperor Gao as the Grand Ancestor and establishing four temples to close ancestors, making five temples.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the reign of Emperor Yuan did Gong Yu, Kuang Heng, and others first debate the rite, taking Emperor Gao as the Grand Ancestor and establishing four temples to direct ancestors, for a total of five.

sentences.zh: 唯劉歆以為天子七廟，諸侯五廟，降殺以兩之義，七者，其正法可常數也。

translations.literal: Only Liu Xin held that the Son of Heaven has seven temples and feudal lords five, the principle of descending reduction by twos—the seven being the proper regular number.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu Xin maintained that the Son of Heaven should have seven temples and feudal lords five, following the principle of reduction by twos at each rank; seven was the proper fixed number.

sentences.zh: 宗不在此數內，有功德則宗之，不可豫設為數也。

translations.literal: "Zong" ancestors are not counted within this number; when there is merit and virtue one makes them zong—they cannot be pre-established as a fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: "Zong" status lies outside this count: ancestors are elevated to zong only when they have merit and virtue—it cannot be prescribed in advance as a fixed number.

sentences.zh: 是以班固稱「考論諸儒之儀，劉歆博而舊矣。

translations.literal: Thus Ban Gu praised: "After examining the rituals of the various Confucians, Liu Xin's interpretation is comprehensive and accords with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Ban Gu wrote: "After weighing the ritual views of the various Confucians, Liu Xin's interpretation is the most comprehensive and truest to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 」光武即位，建高廟於洛陽。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Guangwu took the throne, he built the temple of Emperor Gao in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Guangwu ascended the throne, he built Emperor Gao's temple in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 乃立南頓君以上四廟，就祖宗而為七。

translations.literal: He then established four temples from Lord of Nandun upward, making seven together with the zong and the zu.
translations.idiomatic: He then established four temples reaching back to Lord of Nandun, which together with the zong and zu made seven.

sentences.zh: 至魏初，高堂隆為鄭學，議立親廟四，太祖武帝猶在四親之內，乃虛置太祖及二祧以待後世。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, Gao Tanglong, following Zheng Xuan's school, proposed establishing four temples to close ancestors; Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu was still counted among the four close temples, so they left vacant places for the Grand Ancestor and two distant shrines to await future generations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wei, Gao Tanglong, adhering to Zheng Xuan's school, proposed four temples to direct ancestors; even Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu was still placed among the four close ancestors, and vacant positions were reserved for the Grand Ancestor and two distant shrines for later generations.

sentences.zh: 至景初間，乃依王肅更立六廟，二世祖就四親而為六廟。

translations.literal: By the Jingchu era they followed Wang Su and reestablished six temples, with the Secondary Founding Ancestor added to the four close temples to make six.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jingchu era they followed Wang Su and reorganized the temples into six, adding the Secondary Founding Ancestor to the four close ancestors for a total of six.

sentences.zh: 晉武受禪，博議宗祀，自文帝以上至六世親祖征西府君，而宣帝亦序於昭穆，未升太祖，故祭止六世。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin received the abdication, there was broad debate on ancestral worship; from Emperor Wen upward to the sixth-generation close ancestor, Lord of the Western Expedition Headquarters, and Emperor Xuan was also placed in the zhao-mu sequence without being elevated to Grand Ancestor, so sacrifices extended only to six generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin accepted the abdication, there was extensive debate over ancestral rites. Sacrifices reached back six generations from Emperor Wen to the Western Expedition Headquarters Lord, and Emperor Xuan was placed in the zhao-mu order without being raised to Grand Ancestor, so worship extended only through six generations.

sentences.zh: 江左中興，賀循知禮，至於寢廟之議，皆依魏、晉舊事。

translations.literal: When the south of the Yangzi was restored, He Xun, versed in ritual, in all discussions of temple shrines followed the precedents of Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration of the south, He Xun, who was expert in ritual, followed Wei and Jin precedent in all matters of ancestral temple arrangement.

sentences.zh: 宋武初受命為王，依諸侯立親廟四，即位之後，增祠五世祖相國掾府君、六世祖右北平府君，止於六廟，建身沒主升，亦從昭穆，猶太祖之位也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song first received the mandate as king, following feudal practice he established four temples to close ancestors; after ascending the throne he added worship of his fifth-generation ancestor, the Staff Officer of the Chancellor's Office, and his sixth-generation ancestor, the Lord of Right Beiping, stopping at six temples; upon his own death he was elevated to zu, also following zhao-mu order, occupying the position of Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song first received investiture as king, he established four temples to direct ancestors according to feudal practice. After taking the throne he added sacrifices to his fifth-generation ancestor, the Chancellor's Office Staff Officer, and his sixth-generation ancestor, the Right Beiping Lord, limiting the temples to six. Upon his death he was elevated to zu and placed in the zhao-mu order, occupying the position reserved for the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 降及齊、梁，守而勿革，加宗迭毀，禮無違舊。

translations.literal: Descending to Qi and Liang, they preserved this without change, adding zong and successive destruction, the ritual not departing from old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Through Qi and Liang they preserved this arrangement unchanged, adding zong status and successive abolition without departing from established practice.

sentences.zh: 臣又按姬周自太祖已下，皆別立廟，至於禘祫，俱合食於太祖。

translations.literal: Your subject further notes that from the Grand Ancestor downward the Zhou of Ji surname each had separate temples, yet at the di and xia sacrifices all were jointly offered food at the Grand Ancestor's temple.
translations.idiomatic: I further note that under the Ji Zhou, from the Grand Ancestor downward each ancestor had a separate temple, yet at the great di and xia joint sacrifices all were assembled for offering at the Grand Ancestor's shrine.

sentences.zh: 是以炎漢之初，諸廟各立，歲時常享，亦隨處而祭，所用廟樂，皆像功德而歌舞焉。

translations.literal: Thus at the beginning of the blazing Han, each temple was established separately; at the seasonal regular sacrifices, offerings were also made wherever the temples stood, and the temple music used in each all depicted merit and virtue in song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: Thus at the rise of the Han, each emperor's temple stood separately; seasonal sacrifices were performed at each location, and the music of each temple depicted its honoree's merits in song and dance.

sentences.zh: 至光武乃總立一堂，而群主異室，斯則新承寇亂，欲從約省，自此已來，因循不變。

translations.literal: Only under Emperor Guangwu were all temples gathered into one hall, yet each lord had a separate chamber; this was because, newly succeeding amid the turmoil of brigands, he wished to follow economy and restraint—from that time onward they followed precedent without change.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Emperor Guangwu were all the temples combined into one hall, each ancestor in a separate chamber—because, having just succeeded amid the chaos of rebellion, he sought to economize. From that time forward the arrangement remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 皇隋太祖武元皇帝仁風潛暢，至澤傍通，以昆、彭之勳，開稷、契之緒。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor of Great Sui, Emperor Wuyuan, with benevolent wind subtly pervading and supreme grace reaching everywhere, by the merit of Kun and Peng opened the lineage of Ji and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wuyuan, whose benevolence flowed like a hidden breeze and whose grace reached in every direction, by merits comparable to those of Kun and Peng opened a lineage worthy of Ji and Qi.

sentences.zh: 高祖文皇帝睿哲玄覽，神武應期，撥亂返正，遠肅邇安，受命開基，垂統聖嗣，鴻名冠於三代，寶祚傳於七百。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor Emperor Wen, with penetrating wisdom and mysterious discernment, divine martial spirit responding to the age, putting down disorder and restoring righteousness, pacifying the distant and settling the near, receiving the Mandate and founding the dynasty, bequeathing the succession to sage heirs—his great name surpassing the Three Dynasties, his precious throne transmitted for seven hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor Emperor Wen, with penetrating wisdom and far-reaching vision, divine martial prowess attuned to the times, quelled rebellion and restored order, brought the distant to submission and the near to peace, received the Mandate and founded the dynasty, and bequeathed its succession to worthy heirs—his renown surpassing that of the Three Dynasties, his throne destined to endure for seven hundred years.

sentences.zh: 當文明之運，定祖宗之禮。

translations.literal: Now in this era of civil brilliance, it is time to fix the ritual of zong and zu.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in this age of civil brilliance, it is time to establish the rites governing zong and zu.

sentences.zh: 且損益不同，沿襲異趣，時王所制，可以垂法。

translations.literal: Moreover, reductions and additions differ, and inherited practice takes different directions—the regulation made by the king of the age can be handed down as law.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual has been altered differently in each age, and inherited practice has taken different paths—the institutions established by the sovereign of each age become the standards for posterity.

sentences.zh: 自歷代已來，親用王、鄭二義。

translations.literal: From successive dynasties onward, each in practice has employed the two interpretations of Wang and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty has in practice drawn on the two interpretations of Wang Su and Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 若尋其旨歸，校以優劣，康成止論周代，非謂經通；

translations.literal: If one seeks their essential import and compares their merits and defects, Kangcheng speaks only of the Zhou age—it is not that his interpretation applies universally to the classics;
translations.idiomatic: If one examines their essential meaning and weighs their relative merits, Kangcheng (Zheng Xuan) discusses only the Zhou system—his view is not presented as a universal reading of the classics;

sentences.zh: 子雍總貫皇王，事兼長遠。

translations.literal: Ziyong comprehensively covers all ages from kings to emperors, his scheme embracing both the distant and the long term.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong (Wang Su) encompasses rulers from antiquity through the imperial age, and his scheme serves both immediate needs and long-range ends.

sentences.zh: 今請依據古典，崇建七廟，受命之廟，宜別立廟，祧百世之後，不毀之法。

translations.literal: I now request, following classical precedent, to honorably establish seven temples; the temple of the one who received the Mandate should be separately established, a distant shrine whose temple is not destroyed after a hundred generations—an institution of enduring law.
translations.idiomatic: I now propose, in accordance with classical precedent, the dignified establishment of seven temples. The shrine of the dynastic founder who received the Mandate should stand separately as a distant temple never to be abolished even after a hundred generations—a permanent institution.

sentences.zh: 至於鑾駕親奉，申孝享於高廟；

translations.literal: As for the imperial carriage going in person to perform the offering, displaying filial worship at the High Ancestor's temple;
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven should personally convey offerings to demonstrate filial devotion at the High Ancestor's temple;

sentences.zh: 有司行事，竭誠敬於群主。

translations.literal: the responsible officials performing the rites, exhausting their sincerity in reverence toward the various lords.
translations.idiomatic: while the responsible officials, conducting the ceremonies, should devote their full sincerity in reverence to the various ancestral lords.

sentences.zh: 俾夫規模可則，嚴祀易遵，表有功而彰明德，大復古而貴能變。

translations.literal: Thus the scale would be a model to follow, solemn sacrifice easy to observe, displaying those with merit and making bright virtue manifest, greatly restoring antiquity while honoring the ability to change.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the institutions would serve as a clear model, solemn worship would be easy to maintain, merit would be displayed and bright virtue made manifest, antiquity would be greatly restored, and timely reform would be honored.

sentences.zh: 臣又按周人立廟，亦無處置之文，據冢人職而言之，先王居中，以昭穆為左右。

translations.literal: Your subject further notes that in establishing temples the Zhou people also had no text on placement; according to the office of the Tomb Master, the former kings were placed at the center, with zhao and mu to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: I further note that the Zhou records contain no explicit directions on temple placement; according to the duties of the Tomb Master, the former kings were placed at the center, with zhao and mu arranged to left and right.

sentences.zh: 阮忱所撰《禮圖》，亦從此義。

translations.literal: The Diagrams of Ritual compiled by Ruan Chen also follows this principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Diagrams of Ritual compiled by Ruan Chen likewise follows this principle.

sentences.zh: 漢京諸廟既遠，又不序禘祫。

translations.literal: The various temples in the Han capital were both far apart and did not observe the order of di and xia joint sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han capital the various temples stood far apart and did not follow the prescribed order for di and xia joint sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 今若依周制，理有未安，雜用漢儀，事難全采，謹詳立別圖附之。

translations.literal: If one now follows the Zhou system, there are points where reason is not satisfied; if one mixes in Han practice, the matter is hard to adopt in full—I respectfully submit a separate detailed diagram as an attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Strict adherence to the Zhou system would leave certain difficulties unresolved; mixing in Han practice would make full adoption impracticable. I therefore respectfully submit a separate detailed diagram as an attachment.

sentences.zh: 議未行，尋坐與楊玄感有舊，左遷西海郡司戶。

translations.literal: The proposal was not carried out; soon afterward he was demoted to Registrar of Xihai Commandery on account of old ties with Yang Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was never implemented. Before long he was demoted to Registrar of Xihai Commandery because of his former association with Yang Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 時京兆郡博士潘徽亦以筆札為玄感所禮，降威定縣主簿。

translations.literal: At the time Pan Hui, Erudite of Jingzhao Commandery, was also honored by Xuangan for his literary correspondence and was demoted to Chief Clerk of Weiding County.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pan Hui, an Erudite of Jingzhao Commandery, had also been favored by Xuangan for his literary talents and was demoted to Chief Clerk of Weiding County.

sentences.zh: 當時寇盜縱橫，六親不能相保。

translations.literal: At the time brigands and robbers ran rampant, and even close kin could not protect one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits and rebels roamed everywhere, and even one's closest kin could not ensure one another's safety.

sentences.zh: 亮與同行，至隴山，徽遇病終，亮親加棺斂，瘞之路側，慨然傷懷，遂題詩於隴樹，好事者皆傳寫諷誦，信宿遍於京邑焉。

translations.literal: Liang traveled with him; when they reached Long Mountain, Hui fell ill and died. Liang personally saw to the coffining and burial, interring him by the roadside. Moved with grief, he then inscribed a poem on a tree on Long Mountain; lovers of such things all copied and recited it, and within a night and a day it spread throughout the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was traveling with him. When they reached Long Mountain, Hui fell ill and died. Liang personally prepared his coffin and burial and interred him by the roadside. Deeply grieved, he inscribed a poem on a tree on the mountain. Those who delight in such things copied and recited it, and within two days it had spread throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 薛舉僭號隴西，以亮為黃門侍郎，委之機務。

translations.literal: Xue Ju arrogated the title in Longxi and appointed Liang as Yellow Gate Attendant, entrusting him with critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju declared himself ruler in Longxi and appointed Liang Yellow Gate Attendant, entrusting him with affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 及舉滅，太宗聞亮名，深加禮接，因從容自陳。

translations.literal: When Ju was destroyed, the Prince of Qin heard Liang's name and treated him with deep courtesy; Liang then, at ease, explained himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Ju's defeat, the Prince of Qin heard of Liang and received him with great courtesy. Liang then spoke freely about his circumstances.

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，賜物二百段、馬四匹。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin was greatly pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and four horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin was greatly pleased and rewarded him with two hundred bolts of silk goods and four horses.

sentences.zh: 從還京師，授秦王文學。

translations.literal: Returning with him to the capital, he was appointed Literary Companion to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang returned with him to the capital and was appointed Literary Companion to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 時高祖以寇亂漸平，每冬畋狩。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozu, as the turmoil of brigands gradually subsided, went hunting every winter.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, as the chaos of rebellion gradually subsided, Emperor Gaozu went on winter hunts every year.

sentences.zh: 亮上疏諫曰：「臣聞堯鼓納諫，舜木求箴，茂克昌之風，致昇平之道。

translations.literal: Liang submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your subject has heard that Yao set up a drum to receive remonstrance and Shun erected a wooden marker to seek admonition, flourishing the style of overcoming and prospering and attaining the way of ascending peace.
translations.idiomatic: Liang submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have heard that Yao set up a drum to welcome criticism and Shun placed a wooden post to solicit advice—practices that cultivated the spirit of self-correction and led to an age of peace and prosperity.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下應千祀之期，拯百王之弊，平壹天下，劬勞帝業，旰食思政，廢寢憂人。

translations.literal: Bowing before Your Majesty, who responds to the term of a thousand reigns, rescues the defects of a hundred kings, unifies all under Heaven, toils at the imperial enterprise, eats late while thinking of governance, and forsakes sleep worrying over the people—
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, who meets the demands of an age spanning a thousand reigns, rescues the world from the failures of a hundred rulers, unifies the realm, and labors tirelessly over the imperial enterprise—eating late while pondering governance and forgoing sleep out of concern for the people—

sentences.zh: 用農隙之餘，遵冬狩之禮。

translations.literal: using the leisure between agricultural seasons to observe the ritual of the winter hunt—
translations.idiomatic: devotes the intervals between harvests to observing the ritual of the winter hunt—

sentences.zh: 獲車之所游踐，虞旗之所涉歷，網唯一面，禽止三驅，縱廣成之獵士，觀上林之手搏，斯固畋弋之常規，而皇王之壯觀。

translations.literal: the grounds the hunting chariots traverse, the courses the game wardens' banners mark out, nets open on only one side, game stopped after three drives, releasing the hunters of Guangcheng, observing the hand-to-hand combat of Shanglin—these are indeed the regular rules of the chase and the magnificent spectacle of kings and emperors.
translations.idiomatic: the grounds the hunting chariots roam, the terrain the game wardens' banners sweep across, nets deployed on only one side, quarry spared after three chases, skilled huntsmen of Guangcheng unleashed, the hand-to-hand contests of Shanglin put on display—these are indeed the regular rules of the hunt and the magnificent spectacles befitting emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 至於親逼猛獸，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: But as for personally approaching fierce beasts, your subject is privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: But when it comes to personally confronting fierce beasts, I must confess to private misgivings.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 筋力驍悍，爪牙輕捷。

translations.literal: Their sinews and strength are fierce and mighty, their claws and fangs swift and agile.
translations.idiomatic: Their muscles are fierce and powerful, their claws and fangs swift and sharp.

sentences.zh: 連弩一發，未必挫其凶心；

translations.literal: A volley from repeating crossbows, once released, may not break their fierce spirit;
translations.idiomatic: A volley from repeating crossbows may not break their fury;

sentences.zh: 長戟才捴，不能當其憤氣。

translations.literal: a long halberd barely grasped cannot withstand their raging fury.
translations.idiomatic: and a long halberd barely raised may not withstand their charge.

sentences.zh: 雖孟賁抗左，夏育居前，卒然驚軼，事生慮表。

translations.literal: Even with Meng Ben blocking the left and Xia Yu leading the front, if they suddenly bolt in alarm, matters arise beyond what can be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Even with warriors as strong as Meng Ben and Xia Yu in the lead, if the beast suddenly bolts, the consequences may exceed all foresight.

sentences.zh: 如或近起林叢，未填坑谷，駭屬車之後乘，犯官騎之清塵。

translations.literal: If one should spring from nearby thickets, before ravines and gullies can be filled, it might startle the following carriages of the retinue and charge into the dust of the mounted escort.
translations.idiomatic: If a beast should spring from nearby woods before pits and ravines can be secured, it might stampede the carriages following the imperial retinue or breach the escort's cordon.

sentences.zh: 小臣怯懦，私懷顫慄。

translations.literal: Your petty subject, timid and cowardly, privately trembles with fear.
translations.idiomatic: I am a timid man, and I tremble at the thought.

sentences.zh: 陛下以至聖之資，垂將來之教，降情納下，無隔直言。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with the utmost sage character, bequeathing instruction to future ages, lowering yourself to receive subordinates, with no barrier to straightforward speech—
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, possessing the utmost sagely character and setting an example for posterity, humbles yourself to hear your subjects and welcomes frank speech without reservation—

sentences.zh: 臣叨逢明時，遊宦籓邸，身漸榮渥，日用不知，敢緣天造，冒陳丹懇。

translations.literal: your subject has the good fortune to meet this enlightened age, serving in the prince's establishment, his person gradually favored with honors, day by day unaware of his debt, and dares, relying on Heaven's grace, presumptuously to set forth this sincere pleading."
translations.idiomatic: I have been fortunate to serve in this enlightened age at the prince's establishment, where honors have fallen upon me until I take them for granted. Relying on your grace, I dare presumptuously to offer this earnest plea."

sentences.zh: 」高祖甚納之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu greatly accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu received the remonstrance with great approval.

sentences.zh: 太宗每有征伐，亮常侍從，軍中宴筵，必預歡賞，從容諷議，多所裨益。

translations.literal: Whenever the Prince of Qin went on campaign, Liang regularly attended him; at banquets in the army he always shared in the merriment and rewards, and in leisurely discourse and subtle remonstrance contributed much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Prince of Qin went to war, Liang regularly accompanied him. At military banquets he always joined the festivities, and in leisurely conversation and tactful remonstrance he contributed much of value.

sentences.zh: 又與杜如晦等十八人為文學館學士，太宗入居春宮，除太子舍人，遷太子中允。

translations.literal: He was also one of eighteen Literary Hall Academicians with Du Ruhui and others; when the Prince of Qin entered and took up residence in the Eastern Palace, Liang was appointed Secretariat Aide to the Crown Prince and promoted to Palace Secretary to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was also one of the eighteen Literary Hall Academicians along with Du Ruhui and others. When the Prince of Qin became crown prince and moved into the Eastern Palace, Liang was appointed Secretariat Aide to the Crown Prince and subsequently promoted to Palace Secretary to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，為弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he served as an Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhenguan reign he became an Academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 九年，進授員外散騎常侍、封陽翟縣男，拜通直散騎常侍、學士如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was further appointed Extraordinary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, enfeoffed as Baron of Yangdi County, and appointed Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, his position as academician remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was further made Extraordinary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Baron of Yangdi County, and was appointed Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary while retaining his post as academician.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進爵為侯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was advanced in rank to Marquis, with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was raised to Marquis with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後致仕歸於家。

translations.literal: Later he retired from office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he retired and returned home.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸遼東，亮子遂良為黃門侍郎，詔遂良謂亮曰：「昔年師旅，卿常入幕；

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong went to Liaodong, Liang's son Suiliang was Yellow Gate Attendant; the emperor ordered Suiliang to tell Liang: "In years past on campaigns you often entered my tent;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong marched on Liaodong, Liang's son Suiliang was serving as Yellow Gate Attendant. The emperor instructed Suiliang to tell his father: "In years past during my campaigns you often served in my headquarters;

sentences.zh: 今茲遐伐，君已懸車。

translations.literal: now on this distant expedition you have already hung up your carriage."
translations.idiomatic: now on this distant campaign you have already retired."

sentences.zh: 倏忽之間，移三十載，眷言疇昔，我勞如何！

translations.literal: In the blink of an eye thirty years have passed; speaking with affection of days past, how great my toil!
translations.idiomatic: In what seems an instant thirty years have passed. When I think fondly of those earlier days, how deeply I feel the weight of all that has passed!

sentences.zh: 今將遂良東行，想公於朕，不惜一兒於膝下耳，故遣陳離意，善居加食。

translations.literal: Now as I send Suiliang eastward, I imagine that to you, My Lord, I am no more than sparing one son from beneath your knee; therefore I send this to express my parting feelings—take good care of yourself and eat well."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am sending Suiliang east with the army, I know that in your eyes I am simply taking one son from your side. I send this message to express my feelings at our parting—take good care of yourself and eat well."

sentences.zh: 」亮奉表陳謝。

translations.literal: " Liang submitted a memorial expressing thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 及寢疾，詔遣醫藥救療，中使候問不絕。

translations.literal: When he fell gravely ill, an edict dispatched physicians and medicine for treatment, and palace envoys came ceaselessly to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell gravely ill, the emperor sent physicians and medicine, and palace envoys came without cease to inquire after his condition.

sentences.zh: 卒時年八十八。

translations.literal: When he died he was eighty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚悼惜之，不視朝一日，贈太常卿，陪葬昭陵，謚曰康。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong deeply mourned and lamented him, forgoing court for one day, posthumously appointing him Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granting burial at Zhaoling, and giving the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong mourned him deeply, suspended court for a day, posthumously appointed him Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted him burial at Zhaoling, and bestowed the posthumous title Kang ("Peaceful").

sentences.zh: 長子遂賢，守雍王友。

translations.literal: His eldest son Suixian served as Companion to the Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Suixian served as Companion to the Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 次子遂良，自有傳。

translations.literal: His second son Suiliang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Suiliang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 始太宗既平寇亂，留意儒學，乃於宮城西起文學館，以待四方文士。

translations.literal: At the beginning, after the Prince of Qin had pacified the turmoil of brigands, he turned his attention to Confucian learning and thereupon built the Literary Hall west of the palace to await literary men from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Qin had pacified the realm, he turned his attention to Confucian learning and built the Literary Hall west of the palace to welcome scholars from across the land.

sentences.zh: 於是，以屬大行台司勳郎中杜如晦，記室考功郎中房玄齡及於志寧，軍諮祭酒蘇世長，天策府記室薛收，文學褚亮、姚思廉，太學博士陸德明、孔穎達，主簿李玄道，天策倉曹李守素，記室參軍虞世南，參軍事蔡允恭、顏相時，著作佐郎攝記室許敬宗、薛元敬，太學助教蓋文達，軍諮典簽蘇勖，並以本官兼文學館學士。

translations.literal: Thereupon Du Ruhui, Director of Merit in the subordinate Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Director of Evaluation in the Prince's Secretariat, and Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Army Adviser and Libationer; Xue Shou, Prince's Secretariat of the Heavenly Stratagem Office; literary attendants Chu Liang and Yao Sicheng; Erudites of the Imperial Academy Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; Chief Clerk Li Xuandao; Warehouse Clerk of the Heavenly Stratagem Office Li Shousu; Prince's Secretariat staff officer Yu Shinan; staff members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Editorial Assistant and acting Prince's Secretariat Xu Jingzong and Xue Yuanjing; Assistant Erudite of the Imperial Academy Gai Wenda; Army Adviser and Registrar Su Xu—all retained their original posts while additionally serving as Literary Hall Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Du Ruhui, Director of Merit in the subordinate Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Director of Evaluation in the Prince's Secretariat, and Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Army Adviser and Libationer; Xue Shou, Recorder of the Heavenly Stratagem Office; literary attendants Chu Liang and Yao Sicheng; Imperial Academy Erudites Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; Chief Clerk Li Xuandao; Warehouse Clerk of the Heavenly Stratagem Office Li Shousu; Prince's Secretariat staff officer Yu Shinan; staff members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Editorial Assistant and acting Recorder Xu Jingzong and Xue Yuanjing; Imperial Academy Assistant Erudite Gai Wenda; Army Adviser and Registrar Su Xu—all retained their original offices while additionally serving as Literary Hall Academicians.

sentences.zh: 及薛收卒，復征東虞州錄事參軍劉孝孫入館。

translations.literal: When Xue Shou died, Liu Xiaosun, Recording Officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was again summoned to enter the hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Shou's death, Liu Xiaosun, Recording Officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was summoned to join the hall.

sentences.zh: 尋遣圖其狀貌，題其名字、爵裡，乃命亮為之像贊，號《十八學士寫真圖》，藏之書府，以彰禮賢之重也。

translations.literal: Soon afterward portraits of their likenesses were made, their names, styles, and enfeoffments inscribed; Liang was then ordered to compose encomia for the portraits, titled Portraits of the Eighteen Academicians, stored in the library archive, to display the weight placed on honoring the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long their portraits were painted and their names, styles, and enfeoffments inscribed. Liang was then commissioned to write encomia for the portraits. The work was titled Portraits of the Eighteen Academicians and placed in the imperial library to demonstrate the importance the prince attached to honoring men of talent.

sentences.zh: 諸學士並給珍膳，分為三番，更直宿於閣下，每軍國務靜，參謁歸休，即便引見，討論墳籍，商略前載。

translations.literal: All the academicians were supplied with fine fare, divided into three shifts to rotate overnight duty beneath the pavilion; whenever military and state affairs were quiet, after attending audience and returning to rest, they would immediately be summoned for audience to discuss the classics and appraise former records.
translations.idiomatic: All the academicians were provided with fine meals and divided into three shifts to take turns keeping overnight watch at the pavilion. Whenever military and state affairs permitted, after attending court and retiring they would be summoned at once for audience to discuss the classics and examine historical records.

sentences.zh: 預入館者，時所傾慕，謂之「登瀛洲」。

translations.literal: Those admitted to the academy were admired by the age and called "ascending to Penglai."
translations.idiomatic: Those admitted to the academy were admired by their contemporaries and said to be "ascending to Penglai."

sentences.zh: 顏相時兄師古、蘇勖兄子干。

translations.literal: Yan Xiangshi's elder brother Shigu, and Su Xun's elder brother's son Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Also included were Yan Shigu, elder brother of Yan Xiangshi, and Su Gan, son of Su Xun's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 劉孝孫者，荊州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaosun was a native of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun came from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖貞，周石台太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Shitai under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had been Administrator of Shitai under the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 孝孫弱冠知名，與當時辭人虞世南、蔡君和、孔德紹、庾抱、庾自直、劉斌等登臨山水，結為文會。

translations.literal: Xiaosun was famous at the capping age; with the literary men of the time—Yu Shinan, Cai Junhe, Kong Deshao, Yu Bao, Yu Zizhi, Liu Bin, and others—he climbed mountains and rivers and formed a literary society.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun was already famous when he came of age. With the leading writers of the day—Yu Shinan, Cai Junhe, Kong Deshao, Yu Bao, Yu Zizhi, Liu Bin, and others—he visited scenic mountains and rivers and formed a literary society.

sentences.zh: 大業末，沒於王世充，世充弟偽杞王辯引為行台郎中。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he fell into the hands of Wang Shichong; Shichong's younger brother, the false Prince of Qi Bian, appointed him Attendant of the Mobile Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign he fell into the hands of Wang Shichong. Shichong's younger brother, the false Prince of Qi Bian, appointed him Attendant of the Mobile Court.

sentences.zh: 洛陽平，辯面縛歸國，眾皆離散，孝孫猶攀援號慟，追送遠郊，時人義之。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, Bian was bound and sent back to the state; the multitude all scattered, yet Xiaosun still clung to him weeping and wailing, following to send him off in the distant suburbs. People of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was pacified, Bian was bound and sent back to the Tang. Everyone else scattered, but Xiaosun still clung to him, weeping and wailing, and followed to send him off far into the suburbs. People of the time praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 武德初，歷虞州錄事參軍，太宗召為秦府學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he served as Army Assistant in the Records Office of Yuzhou; Taizong summoned him as a scholar of the Prince of Qin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude he served as Army Assistant in the Records Office of Yuzhou. Taizong summoned him as a scholar of the Prince of Qin's establishment.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，遷著作佐郎、吳王友。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he was promoted to Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and Friend of the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he was promoted to Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and Friend of the Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 嘗采歷代文集，為王撰《古今類序詩苑》四十捲。

translations.literal: He once gathered collected works from successive dynasties and compiled for the prince the forty-scroll Garden of Poetry Arranged by Category, Ancient and Modern.
translations.idiomatic: He once gathered literary collections from successive dynasties and compiled for the prince the forty-scroll Garden of Poetry Arranged by Category, Ancient and Modern.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷本府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Army Adviser in the same establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Army Adviser in the same establishment.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子洗馬，未拜卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent but died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent but died before he could take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 李玄道者，本隴西人也，世居鄭州，為山東冠族。

translations.literal: Li Xuandao was originally from Longxi but his family had long resided in Zhengzhou and was a leading clan of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuandao was originally from Longxi, but his family had long resided in Zhengzhou and ranked among the leading clans of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 祖瑾，魏著作佐郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jin was Assistant in the Bureau of Composition under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jin had been Assistant in the Bureau of Composition under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父行之，隋都水使者。

translations.literal: His father Xingzhi was Commissioner of Waterways under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingzhi had been Commissioner of Waterways under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 玄道仕隋為齊王府屬。

translations.literal: Xuandao served the Sui as an aide in the establishment of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandao served the Sui as an aide in the establishment of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 李密據洛口，引為記室。

translations.literal: When Li Mi held Luokou, he recruited him as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi held Luokou, he recruited Xuandao as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 及密破，為王世充所執。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, he was seized by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was defeated, Xuandao was seized by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 是時，同遇凶俘者並懼死，達曙不寐，唯玄道顏色自若，曰：「死生有命，非憂能了。

translations.literal: At that time those who together met violent capture all feared death and did not sleep until dawn; only Xuandao's countenance was as usual. He said: "Life and death have their mandate; worry cannot settle them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time those captured with him all feared death and could not sleep until dawn. Only Xuandao's countenance remained calm. He said: "Life and death have their mandate; worry cannot settle them.

sentences.zh: 」同拘者雅推其識量。

translations.literal: " Those detained with him greatly admired his insight and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: " Those detained with him greatly admired his insight and composure.

sentences.zh: 及見世充，舉措不改其常。

translations.literal: When he saw Shichong, his conduct and bearing did not change from the usual.
translations.idiomatic: When he was brought before Shichong, his conduct and bearing did not change from the usual.

sentences.zh: 世充素知其名，益重之，釋縛以為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Shichong had long known his name and valued him all the more; he released his bonds and appointed him Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had long known his reputation and valued him all the more. He released his bonds and appointed him Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.

sentences.zh: 東都平，太宗召為秦王府主簿、文學館學士。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, Taizong summoned him as Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qin's establishment and Scholar of the Literary Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, Taizong summoned him as Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qin's establishment and Scholar of the Literary Academy.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，累遷給事中，封姑臧縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Within the Gates and enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Within the Gates and enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang.

sentences.zh: 時王君廓為幽州都督，朝廷以其武將不習時事，拜玄道為幽州長史，以維持府事。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Junkuo was Protector-General of Youzhou; the court, considering him a military man unversed in current affairs, appointed Xuandao Long-Term Administrator of Youzhou to maintain the establishment's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Junkuo was Protector-General of Youzhou. The court, considering him a military man unversed in current affairs, appointed Xuandao Long-Term Administrator of Youzhou to maintain the establishment's affairs.

sentences.zh: 君廓在州屢為非法，玄道數正議裁之。

translations.literal: Junkuo in the province repeatedly acted unlawfully; Xuandao many times corrected him with upright deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Junkuo in the province repeatedly acted unlawfully, and Xuandao many times corrected him with upright deliberation.

sentences.zh: 嘗又遺玄道一婢，玄道問婢所由，雲本良家子，為君廓所掠，玄道因放遣之，君廓甚不悅。
