translations.literal: Once he also sent Xuandao a maid servant; Xuandao asked where the maid came from. She said she was originally from a good family and had been seized by Junkuo. Xuandao therefore released and sent her away, and Junkuo was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Junkuo also sent Xuandao a maid servant. Xuandao asked where she came from, and she said she was originally from a good family and had been seized by Junkuo. Xuandao therefore released her and sent her away, and Junkuo was very displeased.

sentences.zh: 後遇君廓入朝，房玄齡即玄道之從甥也，玄道附書，君廓私發，不識草字，疑其謀己，懼而奔叛，玄道坐流巂州。

translations.literal: Later, when Junkuo entered court, Fang Xuanling was Xuandao's cousin on the mother's side. Xuandao attached a letter; Junkuo opened it privately, could not read cursive script, suspected a plot against himself, feared and fled in rebellion, and Xuandao was banished to Juanzhou on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Junkuo entered court, Fang Xuanling, Xuandao's cousin on the mother's side, was there. Xuandao attached a letter to Fang, but Junkuo opened it privately. Unable to read cursive script, he suspected a plot against himself, fled in rebellion out of fear, and Xuandao was banished to Juanzhou on account of it.

sentences.zh: 未幾征還，為常州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back and appointed Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned back and appointed Prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 在職清簡，百姓安之，太宗下詔褒美，賜以綾彩。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and simple; the common people were at ease. Taizong issued an edict praising him and bestowed silks.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was pure and simple, and the common people were at ease. Taizong issued an edict praising him and bestowed silks.

sentences.zh: 三年，表請致仕，加銀青光祿大夫，以祿歸第，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized requesting retirement; he was given the additional title Silver Gleam Grand Master of Glory, returned home on salary, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized requesting retirement. He was given the additional title Silver Gleam Grand Master of Glory, returned home on salary, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 子雲將，知名。

translations.literal: His son Yunjiang was well known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yunjiang was well known.

sentences.zh: 官至尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the office of Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李守素者，趙州人，代為山東名族。

translations.literal: Li Shousu was a native of Zhaozhou; for generations his family was a famous clan of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shousu came from Zhaozhou. For generations his family had been a famous clan of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 太宗平王世充，征為文學館學士，署天策府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Taizong pacified Wang Shichong, he was summoned as Scholar of the Literary Academy and appointed Army Assistant in the Bureau of Granaries of the Heavenly Stratagem establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong pacified Wang Shichong, he was summoned as Scholar of the Literary Academy and appointed Army Assistant in the Bureau of Granaries of the Heavenly Stratagem establishment.

sentences.zh: 守素尤工譜學，自晉宋已降，四海士流及諸勳貴華戎閥閱，莫不詳究，當時號為「行譜」。

translations.literal: Shousu was especially skilled in genealogy; from Jin and Song down, the scholar-official streams of the four seas and the pedigrees of meritorious nobles, Chinese and barbarian, he investigated in detail. At the time he was called "Walking Genealogy."
translations.idiomatic: Shousu was especially skilled in genealogy. From Jin and Song down, he investigated in detail the pedigrees of scholar-officials throughout the realm and of meritorious nobles, Chinese and barbarian alike. At the time he was called "Walking Genealogy."

sentences.zh: 嘗與虞世南共談人物，言江左、山東，世南猶相酬對；

translations.literal: He once discussed persons of note with Yu Shinan. When speaking of the lands east and south of the Yangzi, Shinan could still respond in turn;
translations.idiomatic: He once discussed persons of note with Yu Shinan. When speaking of the lands east and south of the Yangzi, Shinan could still respond in turn;

sentences.zh: 及言北地諸侯，次第如流，顯其世業，皆有援證，世南但撫掌而笑，不復能答，嘆曰：「行譜定可畏。

translations.literal: when it came to the feudal lords of the northern lands, Shousu proceeded in order like flowing water, displaying their hereditary achievements, all with supporting evidence. Shinan only clapped his hands and laughed, no longer able to answer, and sighed: "Walking Genealogy is truly formidable.
translations.idiomatic: but when it came to the feudal lords of the northern lands, Shousu proceeded in order like flowing water, displaying their hereditary achievements with supporting evidence for each. Shinan only clapped his hands and laughed, no longer able to answer, and sighed: "Walking Genealogy is truly formidable.

sentences.zh: 」許敬宗因謂世南曰：「李倉曹以善談人物，乃得此名，雖為美事，然非雅目。

translations.literal: " Xu Jingzong therefore said to Shinan: "Attendant Li gained this name because he is skilled at discussing persons of note. Though this is a fine thing, it is not an elegant reputation.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Jingzong therefore said to Shinan: "Attendant Li gained this name because he is skilled at discussing persons of note. Though this is a fine thing, it is not an elegant reputation.

sentences.zh: 公既言成准的，宜當有以改之。

translations.literal: Since you, sir, have become the standard in speech, you ought to have some way to change it.
translations.idiomatic: Since you, sir, have become the standard in such matters, you ought to have some way to change it.

sentences.zh: 」世南曰：「昔任彥升美談經籍，梁代稱為『五經笥』；

translations.literal: " Shinan said: "In former times Ren Yansheng beautifully discussed the classics and the Liang called him 'casket of the Five Classics';
translations.idiomatic: " Shinan said: "In former times Ren Yansheng beautifully discussed the classics, and the Liang called him 'casket of the Five Classics';

sentences.zh: 今目倉曹為『人物誌』可矣。

translations.literal: today let us call Attendant Li 'Record of Persons' and that will do.
translations.idiomatic: today let us call Attendant Li 'Record of Persons,' and that will do.

sentences.zh: 」貞觀初卒。

translations.literal: " He died at the beginning of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: " He died at the beginning of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：劉并州有言：「和氏之璧，不獨耀於郢握；

translations.literal: The historian says: Liu of Bingzhou had a saying: "The jade disk of the He clan does not shine only in the hand of Ying;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Liu of Bingzhou once said: "The jade disk of the He clan does not shine only in the hand of Ying;

sentences.zh: 夜光之珠，何專玩於隋掌？

translations.literal: the night-illuminating pearl—why should it be enjoyed only in the palm of Sui?
translations.idiomatic: why should the night-illuminating pearl be enjoyed only in the palm of Sui?

sentences.zh: 天下之寶，固當與天下共之。

translations.literal: Treasures under heaven ought to be shared with all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures under heaven ought to be shared with all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 」虞永興之從建德，李安平之佐公祏，褚陽翟之依薛舉，蓋大渴不能擇泉而飲，大暑不能擇廕而息耳，非不識其飲憩之所。

translations.literal: " Yu of Yongxing followed Jiande, Li of Anping assisted Gongshi, and Chu of Yangdi relied on Xue Ju—this was like great thirst unable to choose a spring to drink, or great heat unable to choose shade to rest. It was not that they did not know where to drink or rest.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu of Yongxing followed Jiande, Li of Anping assisted Gongshi, and Chu of Yangdi relied on Xue Ju. This was like great thirst that cannot choose a spring to drink from, or great heat that cannot choose shade to rest in. It was not that they did not know where to drink or rest.

sentences.zh: 及文皇帝揭三辰而燭天下，群賢霧集，人之所奉，方得躍鱗天池，擅價春山，為一代之至寶，則所托之勢異也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen raised the three luminaries to illuminate all under heaven, the multitude of worthies gathered like mist—what people upheld—only then could they leap with scales in the heavenly pool and set their price on spring mountains, becoming the supreme treasures of an age. The power they relied upon was different.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen raised the three luminaries to illuminate all under heaven, the multitude of worthies gathered like mist around what the people upheld. Only then could they leap with scales in the heavenly pool and set their price on spring mountains, becoming the supreme treasures of an age. The power they relied upon was different.

sentences.zh: 隋掌郢握，曷有常哉！

translations.literal: The palm of Sui and the hand of Ying—how could there be constancy!
translations.idiomatic: The palm of Sui and the hand of Ying—how could there be constancy!

sentences.zh: 二虞昆仲，文章炳蔚於隋、唐之際；

translations.literal: The two Yu brothers— their literary works blazed splendidly at the juncture of Sui and Tang;
translations.idiomatic: The two Yu brothers wrote with splendid brilliance at the juncture of Sui and Tang;

sentences.zh: 褚河南父子，箴規獻替，洋溢於貞觀、永徽之間。

translations.literal: father and son Chu of Henan— their admonitions and remonstrances overflowed between Zhenguan and Yonghui.
translations.idiomatic: father and son Chu of Henan poured forth admonitions and remonstrances throughout Zhenguan and Yonghui.

sentences.zh: 所謂代有人焉，而三家尤盛。

translations.literal: This is what is called each age having its men, yet these three families were especially flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by each age having its men, yet these three families were especially flourishing.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：猗與文皇，蕩滌蒼昊。

translations.literal: The encomium says: How great is Emperor Wen, who swept clean the azure heavens.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: How great is Emperor Wen, who swept clean the azure heavens.

sentences.zh: 十八文星，連輝炳耀。

translations.literal: Eighteen literary stars, their linked splendor blazing bright.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen literary stars shone with linked splendor.

sentences.zh: 虞、褚之筆，動若有神。

translations.literal: The brushes of Yu and Chu, when they moved, seemed possessed by spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The brushes of Yu and Chu, when they moved, seemed possessed by spirit.

sentences.zh: 安平之什，老而彌新。

translations.literal: The compositions of Anping grew ever fresher with age.
translations.idiomatic: The compositions of Anping grew ever fresher with age.
